The Dublin Riviera is a guided walk back in time to a golden era where local Dún Laoghaire residents and visitors wined and dined in the yacht clubs, restaurants and hotels along the waterfront, and danced in the Pavilion, the ballrooms and the nightclubs. The walk will provide an insight into the symbiotic relationship between the harbour and the town and how this helped Dún Laoghaire to evolve into an elegant, glamorous “Dublin Riviera”.

Waterfront Yacht Clubs and the Royal Visits
The Pavilion and Town Hall
Royal Marine Hotel and Gardens
Haddington House Hotel
Former Seafront hotels on Victoria and Marine Terrace

Meet the Animals across our brand new pens and fields — gentle donkeys, our playful new foal, curious goats, ducks and hens, the cosy Bunny Bungalow & much more. Families can roam from field to field and enjoy the farm like never before.

Enjoy pumpkin carving under parent supervision, spooky crafts, and storytelling with Winnifred the Witch on selected days as she brings Samhain folklore to life.

A family friendly celebration of folklore, farming, and fun — all part of Samhain in the Heartlands and Ireland’s Home of Halloween – Longford & Westmeath.

The Dublin Riviera is a guided walk back in time to a golden era where local Dún Laoghaire residents and visitors wined and dined in the yacht clubs, restaurants and hotels along the waterfront, and danced in the Pavilion, the ballrooms and the nightclubs. The walk will provide an insight into the symbiotic relationship between the harbour and the town and how this helped Dún Laoghaire to evolve into an elegant, glamorous “Dublin Riviera”.

Highlights:
Waterfront Yacht Clubs and the Royal Visits
The Pavilion and Town Hall
Royal Marine Hotel and Gardens
Haddington House Hotel
Former Seafront hotels on Victoria and Marine Terrace
Dún Laoghaire Baths (finish)

Readers are advised to check with the organiser before relying on the details published here.
Address: Harbour Plaza, Harbour Rd, Dún Laoghaire, Dublin

Name: Enamel a Christmas Decoration Workshop: Dublin Stories
Description:
Come and sip on a glass of prosecco while creating your very own beautiful, handmade enamelled Christmas decoration at our Winter in Dublin Workshop. 

Inspired by the magic and character of Dublin, we’ve created a selection of charming designs for you to choose from. You’ll enamel your chosen copper design yourself, experimenting with a variety of colours and shapes to create something completely unique.

Add an extra touch of personality with a little initialled silver disc, personalised just for you and attached to your decoration.

To finish, choose your favourite festive ribbon, box up your creation and take it home with you. Ready to hang on your tree, keep as a special Christmas memento, or give as a thoughtful handmade gift.
Address: 4 South Great George's Street, Dublin, Dublin

Name: Dublin Literary Tour - Morning tour
Description: Dublin has always had a way with words. From poets and playwrights to novelists and storytellers, generations of writers have drawn inspiration from its streets, squares and characters. The tour takes in many iconic – and sometimes surprising – places connected with Dublin’s rich literary heritage and the early development of writing in Ireland. Along the way, discover the stories behind Oscar Wilde, James Joyce, George Bernard Shaw, Charles Dickens, Bram Stoker, Sheridan Le Fanu and many other celebrated writers, as we pass by the streets, homes and landmarks associated with their lives and work.

Name: Hilma af Klint: Artist and Visionary
Description:
Af Klint’s art was profoundly informed by spirituality and her explorations of Rosicrucianism, Theosophy, and Anthroposophy. Like many artists of her time, she sought to make sense of and articulate the modern world.

Hilma af Klint’s spiritual paintings were seldom shown beyond her close circle. Her work remained in storage until the 1980s, largely unknown outside Sweden. This show explores the time and place that shaped her unique artistic vision.

Organised in collaboration with The Hilma af Klint Foundation.

Name: Dark Dublin, Dracula, Bram Stoker & Other Horrors
Description:
Bram Stoker may be Ireland's most famous writer worldwide — even rivalling James Joyce, though that's a debate for another day. Building on a lineage of Irish horror writers, Stoker gave the world Dracula, a tale of devilishness that has gripped the global imagination like no other work of fiction.

This walk explores Stoker's work against his own era and the millennia of Irish stories of evil spirits and our uneasy pact with the Underworld. A thousand years of foreign occupation left Dublin steeped in blood, fear and persecution — darkness that fed the imagination. We'll revel in his predecessors too: Charles Maturin, Joseph Sheridan Le Fanu, and Oscar Wilde, each conjuring their own vision of the Other World.
Venue Name: Tree of Gold, Central Plaza (meeting point)
Address: Dame Street, Temple Bar, Dublin, Dublin

Name: Ballylongford Oyster Festival 2027
Description: Celebrating over 34 years of tradition, this community-driven festival transforms the historic coastal village of Ballylongford into a lively hub of food, music, and entertainment every August Bank Holiday weekend. The Seafood Banquet is the crown jewel of the weekend. This highly popular sit-down dinner features a sumptuous spread of fresh local oysters, mussels, and other seafood delights. Famous for its street competitions, including the breakneck Oyster-Swallowing Contest, the highly competitive Barman's Race, and the "Welly-Drag" racing. Alongside the food, the festival incorporates historical guided walks through Ballylongford's deep heritage landscape, including landmarks like Lislaughtin Abbey and Carrigafoyle Castle.

Name: Halloween & its Creepy Irish Origins
Description:
Want a chilling experience? Not too chilling — we want you entertained, not terrified. But we do venture into the supernatural and the origins behind Halloween customs we still enjoy today.

Halloween began as a Christian overlay on the ancient Irish feast of Samhain. The Celts revered their ancestors — and feared them too. On this night, the veil between worlds thinned and spirits, mostly malevolent, walked the land. People devised tactics to protect themselves, customs that survive today as Halloween traditions.

Irish writers drew on this folklore for their own spectral creations — The Picture of Dorian Gray, Melmoth the Wanderer, Carmilla, and Dracula. We'll dip into it all, and try not to get splashed in blood!

Name: Dún Laoghaire Walking Tours, The Dublin Riviera
Description:
The Dublin Riviera is a guided walk back in time to a golden era where local Dún Laoghaire residents and visitors wined and dined in the yacht clubs, restaurants and hotels along the waterfront, and danced in the Pavilion, the ballrooms and the nightclubs. The walk will provide an insight into the symbiotic relationship between the harbour and the town and how this helped Dún Laoghaire to evolve into an elegant, glamorous “Dublin Riviera”.

Waterfront Yacht Clubs and the Royal Visits
The Pavilion and Town Hall
Royal Marine Hotel and Gardens
Haddington House Hotel
Former Seafront hotels on Victoria and Marine Terrace

The Dublin Riviera is a guided walk back in time to a golden era where local Dún Laoghaire residents and visitors wined and dined in the yacht clubs, restaurants and hotels along the waterfront, and danced in the Pavilion, the ballrooms and the nightclubs. The walk will provide an insight into the symbiotic relationship between the harbour and the town and how this helped Dún Laoghaire to evolve into an elegant, glamorous “Dublin Riviera”.

Waterfront Yacht Clubs and the Royal Visits
The Pavilion and Town Hall
Royal Marine Hotel and Gardens
Haddington House Hotel
Former Seafront hotels on Victoria and Marine Terrace
Dún Laoghaire Baths (finish)

Name: Romantic Dublin with a nod to St Valentine!
Description:
Even through centuries of war, hardship and poverty, Dublin has always found room for love stories that capture the public imagination. Irish mythology, too, is rich with tales of heroic romance between warriors and captivating princesses. This tour winds through the city's hidden corners, uncovering these stories—many with surprisingly tragic endings! We'll also explore Dublin's unexpected connection to St Valentine himself: his mortal remains rest not in Rome, but in a casket within a Dublin church! The tour concludes in a former church, once the site of a notable wedding or two, where you'll enjoy two romantic drinks for the price of one.

Name: Frederick Douglass & His Irish Connections
Description:
Frederick Douglass (1818–1895) was a renowned African American abolitionist, orator, publisher and author—reportedly the most photographed American of the 19th century. 

Recently escaped from slavery, Douglass arrived in Dublin in 1845, staying four months to publish his first autobiography, deliver lectures, and meet activists like Daniel O'Connell. He later made four visits to Belfast in 1846. We'll explore Dublin sites tied to his time here, set against political change: relief for Irish Catholics, yet widespread poverty and a famine gripping the countryside. Douglass was deeply moved by Ireland's underclass and those working to relieve it.

Name: Ireland's Christmas Traditions Walking Tour
Description:
Did the Irish invent Christmas? Not quite—but it's not entirely a myth either! Soak up the festive atmosphere amid twinkling lights, beautifully decorated shop windows, public cribs, and a few modest street markets on this engaging walking tour. Discover St Nicholas's surprising Irish connections too. 

The tour ends in the most unusual of Christmas venues—a former historic church, now an iconic cafe/bar—where you can enjoy a festive drink (two for one, our Christmas gift to you). With Dublin's northerly latitude, darkness falls from 3:30pm in December, and that's when the city's magic truly begins.

Name: Ballylongford Oyster Festival 2027
Description: Celebrating over 34 years of tradition, this community-driven festival transforms the historic coastal village of Ballylongford into a lively hub of food, music, and entertainment every August Bank Holiday weekend. The Seafood Banquet is the crown jewel of the weekend. This highly popular sit-down dinner features a sumptuous spread of fresh local oysters, mussels, and other seafood delights. Famous for its street competitions, including the breakneck Oyster-Swallowing Contest, the highly competitive Barman's Race, and the "Welly-Drag" racing. Alongside the food, the festival incorporates historical guided walks through Ballylongford's deep heritage landscape, including landmarks like Lislaughtin Abbey and Carrigafoyle Castle.

Name: Cathedral View Supper Club - Harvest Food Festival
Description:
Our carefully curated multi-course menu showcases the very best of autumn, with ingredients sourced from local farmers, growers, and artisan producers.

Set in the welcoming surroundings of the Temperance Hall, the Harvest Supper Club invites you to slow down, savour each course, and enjoy an evening of conversation, laughter, and shared experiences. As Ireland proudly embraces its place as the Home of Halloween, there is no better way to begin the season than by returning to where it all began - with harvest, hospitality, storytelling, and a table filled with the fruits of our labour.

Brought to you by Samhain in the Heartlands, part of Ireland Home of Halloween. Go to Samhain in the Heartlands website for the full programme.
Address: Temperance Hall, New St, Townparks, Longford

Name: Smoke and Spirits at Fore Distillery
Description:
Discover the stories behind Ireland's original Halloween through immersive storytelling, live music and fascinating insights into the historic art of distillation. 

Celebrating the deep connections between Ireland's heritage, storytelling and age-old crafts, Smoke & Spirits offers visitors a warm and memorable autumn evening in one of Westmeath's most distinctive locations. With refreshments available to purchase, it's the perfect opportunity to experience the magic, mystery and traditions of Samhain in the heart of the Midlands.

Brought to you by Samhain in the Heartlands, part of Ireland Home of Halloween. Go to Samhain in the Heartlands website for the full programme.

Name: From First Harvest to Final Feast: A Time Traveller's Roleplaying Adventure Through the Harvest Season
Description:
Between Lughnasa, the festival of Lugh and the first harvest, and Samhain, the threshold of winter when the veil between worlds grows thin, lies the story of how people have lived, gathered, feared, and celebrated the harvest across ages. 

Created in collaboration between Dún na SÍ and the Midlands Adventurers Guild, this immersive experience invites participants to discover what harvest has meant across generations of Irish life through an interactive, creative, and entertaining roleplaying game.

Name: The Man Who Swallowed a Dictionary
Description:
Green Shoot Productions presents The Man Who Swallowed a Dictionary, a powerful one-man drama about the life, language and legacy of David Ervine.

Written by Robert Niblock with Martin Lynch and Matthew McElhinney, the play looks beyond the headlines to reveal the human story behind Ervine’s transformation.
Loaded with Belfast humour, moving and politically charged, The Man Who Swallowed a Dictionary explores identity, class, family, conflict and the possibility of change. For Dublin audiences, it offers a distinctive Northern Irish Protestant perspective on a period of history that reshaped relationships and politics across the island, while remaining a human story.

“Beautifully written… superbly acted by Paul Garrett.” – Irish News

Name: The Man Who Swallowed a Dictionary
Description:
Green Shoot Productions presents The Man Who Swallowed a Dictionary, a powerful one-man drama about the life, language and legacy of David Ervine.

Written by Robert Niblock with Martin Lynch and Matthew McElhinney, the play looks beyond the headlines to reveal the human story behind Ervine’s transformation.
Loaded with Belfast humour, moving and politically charged, The Man Who Swallowed a Dictionary explores identity, class, family, conflict and the possibility of change. For Dublin audiences, it offers a distinctive Northern Irish Protestant perspective on a period of history that reshaped relationships and politics across the island, while remaining a human story.

“Beautifully written… superbly acted by Paul Garrett.” – Irish News
Address: Smock Alley Theatre, 1662, 6-7 Exchange Street Lower, Temple Bar, Dublin, Dublin

Name: Remember That Time? A Musical
Description:
Remember That Time? is an uplifting one-woman musical about loss, change and resilience.

After a breakup, a heartbroken musician returns to her native Dublin after 25 years away to reclaim her identity and passion for life.
A humorous, deeply personal and moving story, with original songs woven throughout.

Featuring onscreen performances by Gearoid Farrelly and Naimee Coleman.

Winner – Edinburgh Fringe Theatre Award 2025
Winner – Best Performance, International Dublin Gay Theatre Festival 2024

The Dublin Riviera is a guided coastal walk back to a golden era where local residents and visitors wined and dined in the yacht clubs, restaurants and hotels along the waterfront, and danced in the Pavilion, the ballrooms and the nightclubs. The walk will provide an insight into the symbiotic relationship between the harbour and the town and how this helped Dún Laoghaire to evolve into an elegant and glamorous centre of hospitality, entertainment and luxurious bathing, a “Dublin Riviera”.

Name: Crash Course On Ireland
Description:
Crash Course on Ireland is a fun and informal two-hour introduction to Irish history and culture, presented by two qualified local tour guides in a traditional Dublin pub.

Over a pint, discover the big stories that shaped Ireland – from the Celts, Vikings and Normans through the Famine, 1916, independence and modern Ireland. Along the way, explore Irish music, sport, writers, language, pub culture and some of the quirks of Irish life that visitors often notice but don't quite understand.

Experience this powerful new play at the Abbey Theatre from 25 November - 30 January 2027.

Name: Gaillimh Ah-Boo! Luxmuralis
Description:
Created by sculptor Peter Walker and composer David Harper, the installation transforms the ancient stone architecture into a canvas of color, narrative, and sound.

Light & Projection: Fine art imagery and vibrant light projections paint the vaulted ceilings, arches, and historic stonework, mirroring the feel of "stained glass windows of our time."

Soundscapes: Bespoke, atmospheric musical compositions resonate throughout the nave, accentuating the acoustics of the 14th-century interior.

Self-Guided Walkthrough: Visitors journey through the building at their own pace.

Funded through the Galway City Council Night-Time Economy and Gaillimh Ah-Boo! Programme and the Department of Culture, Communications and Sport.

Name: Dún Laoghaire Walking Tours 2027, The Dublin Riviera shore excursion
Description:
The Dublin Riviera is a guided coastal walk back to a golden era where local residents and visitors wined and dined in the yacht clubs, restaurants and hotels along the waterfront, and danced in the Pavilion, the ballrooms and the nightclubs. The walk will provide an insight into the symbiotic relationship between the harbour and the town and how this helped Dún Laoghaire to evolve into an elegant and glamorous centre of hospitality, entertainment and luxurious bathing, a “Dublin Riviera”.

Meeting Point:
Beside cruise passenger drop-off point at Quarterdeck

Highlights:
Waterfront Yacht Clubs and Royal Visits
The Pavilion and Town Hall
Royal Marine Hotel and Gardens
Haddington House Hotel
Former Seafront hotels 
Dún Laoghaire Baths
Address: Harbour Plaza, Harbour Rd, Dún Laoghaire, Dublin

Name: Macnas Parade - Fiáin - 40th Anniversary Halloween Parade
Description:
The main anchor event of Galway's Gaillimh Ah-Boo! Samhain celebrations as part of Failte Ireland's 'Home of Halloween' programme, Galway based award winning theatre company Macnas are inviting everyone to join in the spectacle of their 40th Anniversary Parade which will be bigger than ever.

Fiáin (fee-awn) is a celebration of the wild - the wild elements of the West of Ireland, the wild inspirations that have imbued our work over the last 40 years, and the wild energy that engulfs the streets, performers and audiences as we own the streets and public spaces for one night only.

Readers are advised to check with the organiser before relying on the details published here.
Address: Galway City, Galway

Name: Adrift
Description:
A rural Irish family gathers to celebrate a birthday, but tensions quickly rise when they confront one sister’s relationship with a refugee. Fierce, funny and immediate, Deirdre Kinahan’s ADRIFT explores fear, belonging and Ireland’s complicated relationship with emigration and immigration. Taking the arguments that divide communities and bringing them into the heart of an Irish kitchen, this contemporary family drama is both deeply human and unsettling. Directed by Marc Atkinson Borrull and featuring a stellar cast, ADRIFT promises an honest and thought-provoking night at the theatre.

Address: Backstage Theatre, Farneyhoogan, Farranyoogan, Longford

Name: Aindrais De Staic & The Latchikos
Description:
Aindrais de Staic return with his distinctive mix of storytelling, music, comedy and spoken word to Valentine's, Longford, alongside The Latchikos, whose lively blend of Balkan, Roma, Irish and world music has made them a favourite with audiences across the country. 

Together they create a performance that combines original songs, colourful stories, humour and exceptional musicianship. No two shows are quite the same, with plenty of room for improvisation and audience interaction along the way. 

Part of Ireland Home of Halloween programme, bringing together music, storytelling and performance in a relaxed and intimate setting.

Suitable for +16

Description:
With Shona’s wide range of skills in art and illustration and her engaging style, this is a wonderful opportunity for young artists to delve into their own imaginations and discover the depths of their creativity. Description:
An award-winning illustrator and author based in Co. Waterford, Shona creates unique characters and mystical worlds that fire the imaginations of children and adults alike.

Name: Samhain na mBan
Description:
Women's roles in traditional celebrations will be expressed through song, music, storytelling, ritual, arts, conversation, craft-making and other forms of creative expression. The event celebrates the traditions of Samhain and lá na marbh celebrations from other cultures, such as the Día de los Muertos (Mexico). Áras nan Gael will be decorated in handmade, indigenous symbols relating to Samhain and the celebration of the dead in other cultures.

Name: Gaillimh Ah-Boo! Rituals of the Sidhe
Description:
At its heart is the promenade performance Rituals of the Sídhe – Galway Between Worlds, an immersive theatrical journey through the Circle of Life National Organ Donor commemorative Garden in Salthill. The work invites audiences on a journey through a series of interconnected ritual encounters where the boundaries between worlds begin to dissolve. 

The audience is guided throughout the experience by Hugh W. Brown performing as Painseo Sweeney, a wandering storyteller, threshold keeper, trickster, ritual guide, and master of ceremonies who leads the gathering through myth, memory, celebration, danger, wonder, and transformation.

Name: At the Threshold: A Samhain Art Exhibition & Sensory experience
Description:
The event begins with a welcoming art exhibition at the front of the Croílar building, featuring both two and three dimensional work. Visitors are then invited into the Transitional Samhain Sensory Tunnel, located along Croílar’s long internal hallway. Inspired by Samhain as a time between light and dark, the tunnel is a calm, immersive experience using projected artwork, soft lighting, recorded sound from the Croílar choir, and tactile textile panels. 

The experience is engaging without being overwhelming and is designed with clear choices, gentle transitions, and no sudden sensory changes.

Name: Gaillimh Ah-Boo! Gan Múchadh
Description:
Step into a world of mesmerizing light and warmth as Galway reclaims its Celtic heritage for the Gaillimh Ah-Boo! festival. Blending high-energy circus arts, dangerous object manipulation, and cutting-edge visual technology, this vibrant fire and LED performance brings the ancient spirit of Samhain straight to the city’s historic medieval streets.  

Designed to delight audiences of all ages, the act balances high-octane spectacle with warm, family-friendly charm. Striking blazing flames and intricate, glowing LED patterns create an unforgettable visual narrative that embodies the wild artistic energy Galway is celebrated for around the globe.

Experience the magic of Dublin during the festive season on our Winter Lights City Tour! 

Sit back, relax and enjoy a journey through Dublin’s beautifully illuminated streets and landmarks as the city comes alive with festive lights and decorations.

Take in the atmosphere, admire the sparkling lights and enjoy Dublin from a different perspective as you discover the city after dark. Whether you’re visiting Dublin for the first time or seeing it with fresh eyes, the Winter Lights City Tour is a wonderful way to experience the festive charm of the capital.

Tours at 7pm & 8.30pm.

Readers are advised to check with the organiser before relying on the details published here.
Address: 13 O'Connell Street Upper, North City, Dublin

Name: Stupid August
Description:
A silent historical fantasy, which tells the story of an amnesiac clown exiled to 1960s Ireland, whose buried memories slowly resurface, forcing him to confront the ghosts of the past. Stupid August utilizes elements of fact and conjecture and mixes them in a hybrid of expressionism, surrealism and pantomime. Drawing on unsettling historical events — including the arrival of Nazi war criminals in Ireland, the film explores the dangers of burying collective histories. 

Funded under the Arts Council of Ireland's Authored Works Award. 

The screening on Sunday 27 September at 4:10pm will be followed by Q&A with director Padraig Trehy
Address: Triskel Arts Centre, Tobin St, Centre, Cork

Name: Everybody Digs Bill Evans
Description:
1961. Bill Evans is playing with what he considers the perfect musical trio until tragedy strikes in the premature death of his bass player, Scott LaFaro - his musical soulmate. Traumatised by grief, Evans stops playing for the first time since his childhood. A tug-of-war between personal torment and the seemingly safer haven of familial love will see Evans oscillate between New York and suburbia, his genius always bubbling beneath the surface. EVERYBODY DIGS BILL EVANS is a biographical drama film about the jazz pianist and composer, written by Mark O’Halloran and based on Owen Martell's novel Intermission. Shot in a mixture of black-and-white and saturated colour, director Grant Gee presents multiple timelines to illustrate Evans’ life.

Name: Raja Quartet – A World of Quartets
Description:
Prokofiev’s first string quartet was first performed in 1931. This wonderful quartet combines music of exuberant brilliance with gorgeous tunes and a deep, expressive melancholy.

Webern’s Langsamer Satz is a beautiful and passionate love song to his future wife.

Aloys Fleischmann wrote his Movement for String Quartet while a student at University College, Cork 1927-1932.

Ginastera’s stunning first string quartet is still one of the great unknowns in the quartet repertoire. Rooted in the rhythmic energy of Argentinian folk tradition this is wild and thrilling music.

Name: ECM 2026: Rolf Lislevand
Description:
Virtuoso of the lute and Baroque guitar Rolf Lislevand is one of the most charismatic figures in today’s early music scene. He was born in Oslo in 1961 and studied classical guitar at the Norwegian State Academy of Music from 1980 to 1984. He continued his studies with Hopkinson Smith and Eugène Dombois at the Schola Cantorum Basiliensis in Switzerland and later played with several of Jordi Savall’s ensembles.

What lives beneath the surface of Ireland’s coastline — and how can we learn to see it? Name: In Conversation with Louise O'Neill on A Bigger Life
Description:
Louise O’Neill is undoubtedly one of Ireland’s most acclaimed contemporary authors. Her complex, sharp novels, including Only Ever Yours, Asking for It and After the Silence, have earned her praise at home and internationally. A Bigger Life marks a departure from her previous work as her first full-length memoir.

Description:
Join Colm O’Regan and Páraic Kerrigan for a warm, witty and wonderfully Irish conversation inspired by their new books. Name: EPIC x Jeanie Combo Ticket
Description:
Take a journey back in time, get an insight into life on board a Famine ship and hear the stories of the people who made the arduous voyage.

Then head into EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum to discover what happened to those who left, and the huge global impact they managed to have all over the world. 

Your experience begins at the Jeanie, and you’re free to explore EPIC at your own pace afterwards. The Jeanie is located two minutes from EPIC.

Tours occur between 10am and 3.30pm every 30 minutes - a guided Jeanie tour takes 50 minutes while visitors should leave themselves 90 minutes to explore EPIC.

Readers are advised to check with the organiser before relying on the details published here.
Address: The Jeanie Johnston Famine Ship, Custom House Quay, North Wall, Dublin, Dublin

Name: Ideas On Tap (Lectures In Pubs)
Description:
Join Dr Carla Mateus, Lecturer at Maynooth University and former Met Éireann researcher, for a fascinating look at climate change and Ireland’s extreme weather from heatwaves and storms to changing ice sheets and coastal environments.

One night could be about Dublin history, cult movies, or the psychology of personality. Another could explore black holes, political movements, philosophy, true crime, science fiction, or the weird side of human behaviour.

After each talk there’s a live Q&A, drinks, conversation, and a chance to meet new people who are curious about the world.

Over 18s only.

Name: Roddy Doyle and Anne Enright in Conversation
Description:
Both have shaped contemporary Irish literature over the past two decades, producing work that has captivated readers at home and around the world. They join The Irish Times Books Editor Martin Doyle, whose new collection A Hosting: Interviews with Irish Writers 1991–2026 (Lilliput Press) brings together conversations with many of Ireland’s most celebrated writers. Join us for a special conversation about writing, success, and the changing landscape of Irish literature.

Name: Día de los Muertos
Description:
Free, inclusive, family-friendly celebration in the grounds of historic Swords Castle.

Honouring loved ones who have passed, this culturally authentic event celebrates life and togetherness through music, food, art and remembrance. Brought to you by Swords Castle in partnership with the South and Central American Community.

In the restored Chapel see a decorated ofrenda (altar), in memory of recently departed community members. Talks will explain the context and meaning of the celebration.

Indoor storytelling for all. Outdoors enjoy Latin American and South American food, then settle in for a screening of Pixar’s Coco. Performers bring the festival atmosphere to life with music and dance.

Please dress appropriately for an outdoor event.
Address: Swords Castle, Bridge St, Townparks, Swords, Fingal, Dublin

Name: Legends, Ghosts and Ghouls of Dublin | Walking Tour
Description:
Ireland has a unique relationship with its legendary past. Kept alive in the histories of the Filí and the Seanchaidhe, Ireland’s gods were not destroyed but - in the words of Mark Williams - demoted to lesser beings. This is an important element of Ireland’s oral histories, which in turn have coloured its popular histories and left many legends for us to parse over today.

On the other side of Irish history we have the ballrooms, the salons, and the private studies of Dublin’s literati. The seances and unwrapping parties, the mysteries and the macabre, all combining into the secret esoteric orders that strove to unlock the secrets of existence.

Name: Halloween Scavenger Hunt
Description:
Centuries ago, a pirate fled through the fog, hiding his treasure as a sea monster rose from the dark waters in pursuit. Name: Philomena Begley & Ray Lynam's Farewell Party
Description:
Philomena Begley & Ray Lynam are true legends of Irish Country music, with glittering careers spanning over six decades. Both have enjoyed countless No.1 hits, including Blanket on the Ground, Gypsy Joe and Me and The Queen of the Silver Dollar, and have performed to packed houses across Ireland, the UK and the USA.

Having shared stages with country greats such as George Jones, Tammy Wynette and Charley Pride, Philomena and Ray are now joining forces for their Farewell Party Tour — their final joint headline run.

Expect classic duets including My Elusive Dreams, We Go Together and Somewhere Between, alongside many more favourites.

A rare opportunity to see two true legends of Country Music together on stage.

Name: Children’s Event: Fangs & Fables
Description:
Visit Waterford Treasures' King of the Vikings to meet Raghnailt, a medieval vampire, and Ulfr, a Viking werewolf, as they battle it out to decide who is the best storyteller – and whose sagas are the scariest. From the legendary Cú Chulainn to fearsome sea monsters of Norse mythology, visitors will discover strange and spine-chilling tales from the past.

Along the way, visitors can handle precious relics, wield fearsome weapons and even try playing the enchanted harp to lull the werewolf to sleep.

The tour offers a fun and atmospheric Halloween experience for families during the midterm break.

Please note: This is a spooky Halloween experience and some content may frighten younger children. Parental discretion is advised.

Name: CHOP!
Description:
Axes chop. Wood flies. Egos splinter.

CHOP! is a dangerously funny, wildly absurd descent into fragile masculinity, environmental collapse, and the insatiable hunger for more. Expect real danger, real questions, zero solutions and a lot of laughs.

This is the kind of show you come out buzzing from: funny, physical, slightly dark, and full of heart. At its centre is a lone wood-chopper stuck in a strange, end-of-the-world loop, hacking away as everything around him falls apart.

Blending slapstick, clowning, and high-energy physical comedy with real axes and real wood chopping! CHOP! turns eco-anxiety, masculinity, and our messy relationship with the planet into a fast, joyful, and surprisingly moving experience.

Highlights include the Michael Hartnett Poetry Award, live music, poetry events, a colourful EU parade and activities for all ages. Many events are free, with advance booking recommended for some.

📍 Located in Carlingford, approximately one hour from Dublin and Belfast.

Name: Art by the Sea – Guided Walk on Stories of Irish Artists, Writers and Visionaries
Description: Enjoy a unique guided walking trail along Scotsman’s Bay, from Sandycove to Dún Laoghaire and back, taking time to admire the beautiful seascapes while listening to stories of iconic, literary and artistic figures (artists, writers, creatives) associated with Dún Laoghaire-Rathdown and the surrounding areas, including Sarah Purser, James Joyce, J.M. Synge, the Yeats sisters, Samuel Beckett and Maeve Binchy. The tour begins and ends at the Smashing Times Visual Art Gallery, where participants can enjoy a vibrant exhibition and continue the conversation through visual art and creative practice.  Tickets: Adults €15.  Under 18 €5. Under 3 go free
Address: 30 Sandycove Road, Sandycove, Dublin

Name: Studio Songs by Daughter Of A Drum with Aoife Ó Tiompánaigh – Performance and Artist Talk
Description: A workshop and performance by multidisciplinary artist Aoife Ó Tiompánaigh, presented as part of the inaugural Smashing Times Artist Residency Programme. The residency provides time, space and support for research, experimentation and development of artistic practice, with the public event forming part of the artist’s creative exploration. Aoife is a multidisciplinary artist working in contemporary dance, choreography, filmmaking, music and education.
Address: 30 Sandycove Road, Sandycove, Dublin

Name: Wicklow Stories Film Festival 2026
Description:
The Wicklow Stories Film Festival returns to the Whale Theatre in Greystones on Friday, 13 November 2026, celebrating filmmaking, storytelling and the landscapes of County Wicklow.
Established in 2022, this annual independent short film festival showcases films with a strong connection to Wicklow, whether through their filming locations, filmmakers or stories. The live screenings bring film fans, emerging talent and industry professionals together to discover a diverse selection of short films, each under 22 minutes.
Now in its fifth year, the festival offers a great opportunity to experience local creativity on the big screen and discover Wicklow through the eyes of filmmakers.
Address: Whale Theatre, Meridian Point, Theatre Ln, Adjacent, Greystones, Wicklow

Name: Oíche Filíochta le Laoighseach Ní Choisdealbha – Poetry Readings | Artist Talk | Chat |Audience Q&A
Description: An Irish-language poetry evening with Laoighseach Ní Choisdealbha, a poet and writer and The Arts Council Scríbhneoir Cónaithe Gaeilge at Dublin City University (DCU). The programme features poetry readings in Irish and an informal discussion with the artist about her work followed by an audience Q&A in both Irish and English. Presented by the Smashing Times Aisling Programme promoting Irish language drama and performance and celebrating the Irish language and the power of the arts to promote equality, human rights and diversity. Supported by Foras na Gaeilge.
Address: 30 Sandycove Road, Sandycove, Dublin

Name: The Weight of Return – Multidisciplinary Art featuring Installation and Live Monologue Performance
Description: A multidisciplinary installation and live monologue presented by Peace Bridges International and Udeido Collective. The work commemorates approximately 120,000 internally displaced people in the highlands of West Papua and uses art to explore displacement, conflict, cultural identity and the struggle to return home. Presented by Costan Fakrian Raharusun, Artist and Teacher and Samuel Yohanes Glenn, Artist and Cultural Craftsman.
Address: 30 Sandycove Road, Sandycove, Dublin

Name: Workshop on Feminist Utopias – Imagining Alternative Futures
Description: An applied-theatre and participatory workshop led by Ekaterina Schalmann, theatre artist, drama teacher and researcher,  and Evdokia Romanova (aka Duniam, an ntersectional Feminist, Community Artist, and Human Rights Activist). Participants are invited to imagine alternative feminist futures centred on care, solidarity, equality, ecological and social justice and collective liberation, using creative practices to question existing systems and rehearse more just futures. Presented by FemLink, a Queer, Feminist, Migrant Collective, based in Vienna, Austria
Address: 30 Sandycove Road, Sandycove, Dublin

Name: Roscommon International Film Festival 2026
Description:
Roscommon International Film Festival returns to Roscommon Arts Centre on 23 and 24 October 2026 for two days celebrating emerging filmmaking and screenwriting talent.
Now in its fourth year, the festival provides a platform for filmmakers from Ireland and around the world, showcasing selected short films across genres including drama, comedy, thriller, horror and documentary. Awards recognise international and Irish talent, with a dedicated category celebrating films with a Roscommon connection.
The festival also brings filmmakers, screenwriters and film lovers together, creating opportunities for networking, conversation and collaboration while celebrating original storytelling on screen.

Readers are advised to check with the venue before relying on the details published here.
Address: Roscommon Arts Centre, Circular Rd, Ballypheasan, Roscommon

Name: Fingal Festival of History 2026
Description:
Celebrate 10 years of discovery at the Fingal Festival of History, taking place from 26 September to 11 October 2026.

Explore a programme of 19 free events across Fingal’s libraries and heritage venues, with talks covering local, Irish and international history. Topics range from the disappearance of Agatha Christie and Ireland’s links with the American Revolution to the 1926 Census, Balbriggan Harbour and fascinating stories from Fingal’s past.

The programme also includes guided heritage tours in Clonsilla and Rush, while History at the Library Day in Swords explores Ireland’s historical links with Europe and the EU. All events are free, although advance booking is recommended.

Readers are advised to check with the venue before relying on the details published here.
Address: The Carnegie, North St, Townparks, Swords, Dublin

Name: Launch of the Eighth Irish Arts and Human Rights Festival 2026
Description:
Smashing Times Visual Art Gallery and Centre for the Arts and Human Rights, 30 Sandycove Road, Sandycove, Dublin A96V9P1. Admission Free
The opening reception and launch of the eighth annual International Irish Arts and Human Rights Festival, and launch of the Voices of Peace multidisciplinary exhibition. Guest speakers and artists include Barry Ward TD (Festival Patron); Richard Boyd Barrett TD; Alan Glasgow, Executive Director, Front Line Defenders;  and Hina Khan, Voices of Peace Visual Artist. There is an artist talk and poetry reading by Mary Moynihan with live monologue performances by Ciara Hayes, Brendan Heade and Andy Johnson. Followed by refreshments and chat.
Address: 30 Sandycove Road, Sandycove, Dublin

Name: Irish in Resistance During World War II One-Day-Only Pop-Up Installation and Talk
Description: The Irish in Resistance During World War II pop-up installation features 12 storyboard artworks by Mary Moynihan, each telling the story of an Irish person who resisted fascism and totalitarianism and stood up for the rights and dignity of others during WWII. The storyboards are accompanied by original artworks by Hina Khan, Amna Walayat, Jessica Rodrigues, Noah Sex and Mary Moynihan, responding creatively to the stories and themes of courage, resistance, compassion, and human rights. Original poems by novelist, poet and playwright Féilim James are also on display.
Address: 30 Sandycove Road, Sandycove, Dublin

Name: In Conversation: Irish in Resistance during World War II. Storytelling, Poetry and Audience Q&A
Description: In Conversation: Irish in Resistance during World War II. Storytelling, Poetry & Audience Q&A:  Wednesday 14 October 7-9pm at Smashing Times: Ciara Hayes interviews journalist and author Clodagh Finn, author and lawyer John Morgan, and writer, poet and artist Mary Moynihan. Through storytelling, poetry and conversation, the event explores the stories of Irish people in resistance during World War II imcluding Mary Elmes, Katherine ‘Kate’ McCarthy and Samuel Beckett, followed by audience Q&A.
Address: 30 Sandycove Road, Sandycove, Dublin

Name: Smashing Times Arts + Human Rights Film Festival – Screening of Documentaries
Description: A curated programme of short documentaries from Irish and international creators celebrating independent filmmaking and socially engaged storytelling. The event brings filmmakers, artists and audiences together for screenings, conversation and creative exchange.
Address: 30 Sandycove Road, Sandycove, Dublin

Name: Tipperary Dance presents Los Perros
Description:
Tipperary Dance presents Los Perros (The Dogs), a compelling contemporary dance work by Led Silhouette and acclaimed choreographer Marcos Morau at The Source Arts Centre, Thurles, on 8 October 2026.
Performed by Martxel Rodríguez and Jon López, the 50-minute piece explores the fragility of the human body and the isolating effects of life in the digital age. Name: Eugene O’Neill International Festival of Theatre
Description:
The Eugene O’Neill International Festival of Theatre returns to New Ross from 14–18 October 2026, celebrating the Nobel Prize-winning playwright’s Irish heritage through theatre, music and cultural events.
The international programme includes The Unkillable Irishman, O’Neill’s Long Day’s Journey Into Night performed by Georgia’s Tumanishvili Theatre Company, Lucia Joyce by Spain’s Karlik Danza Teatro and Ah, Wilderness!. There’s also a special concert featuring Zoë Conway and John McIntyre, alongside musicians from Ireland, Spain and Georgia. Scholar panels, heritage experiences and a jazz cruise on the River Barrow complete five days celebrating theatre, culture and New Ross’s transatlantic connections.
Address: New Ross, Wexford

Name: Eugene O’Neill International Festival of Theatre
Description:
The Eugene O’Neill International Festival of Theatre returns to New Ross from 14–18 October 2026, celebrating the Nobel Prize-winning playwright’s Irish heritage through theatre, music and cultural events.
The international programme includes The Unkillable Irishman, O’Neill’s Long Day’s Journey Into Night performed by Georgia’s Tumanishvili Theatre Company, Lucia Joyce by Spain’s Karlik Danza Teatro and Ah, Wilderness!. There’s also a special concert featuring Zoë Conway and John McIntyre, alongside musicians from Ireland, Spain and Georgia. Scholar panels, heritage experiences and a jazz cruise on the River Barrow complete five days celebrating theatre, culture and New Ross’s transatlantic connections.
Address: New Ross, Wexford

Name: Éigse Michael Hartnett Literary and Arts Festival
Description:
Éigse Michael Hartnett returns to Newcastle West, Co. Limerick, from 1 to 4 October 2026, celebrating the life and legacy of acclaimed Irish poet Michael Hartnett.

The four-day literary and arts festival brings together poets, writers, musicians, artists and thinkers for a varied programme of readings, conversations, performances, workshops and special events. This year’s programme also has a European flavour, marking Ireland’s Presidency of the Council of the European Union.

Highlights include the Michael Hartnett Poetry Award, live music, poetry events, a colourful EU parade and activities for all ages. Many events are free, with advance booking recommended for some.
Address: Newcastle West, Limerick

Name: Tipperary Town Samhain Festival
Description:
Tipperary Town Samhain Festival brings a night of Halloween fun and entertainment to the heart of Tipperary Town.
Dress up for the occasion and enjoy thrilling rides, fancy dress competitions for children and adults, face painting, mask making and monster hits from DJ Richie. For an extra dose of Halloween atmosphere, brave the Haunted Trail along the Ara Walkway, transformed into one of the spookiest places in town.
The celebrations culminate in a spectacular fireworks display, making this a fun-filled Samhain celebration for families and Halloween fans of all ages. The Haunted Trail is free, but advance registration is required.

Name: Fingal Festival of History 2026
Description:
Celebrate 10 years of discovery at the Fingal Festival of History, taking place from 26 September to 11 October 2026.

Explore a programme of 19 free events across Fingal’s libraries and heritage venues, with talks covering local, Irish and international history. Topics range from the disappearance of Agatha Christie and Ireland’s links with the American Revolution to the 1926 Census, Balbriggan Harbour and fascinating stories from Fingal’s past.

The programme also includes guided heritage tours in Clonsilla and Rush, while History at the Library Day in Swords explores Ireland’s historical links with Europe and the EU. All events are free, although advance booking is recommended.

Name: Strokestown TradFest 2026
Description:
Strokestown TradFest returns from 9–11 October 2026 for a weekend celebrating traditional Irish music, song and dance in Strokestown, Co. Roscommon.

Name: Intercultural Dance Workshops
Description:
Celebrate cultural exchange through movement and dance at Friars’ Gate Theatre in Kilmallock.

Led by experienced traditional dancer and facilitator Ciara Flanagan, these interactive workshops introduce participants to traditional Irish dance styles and rhythms alongside German folk dance.

Separate sessions are tailored for children aged 6–11, teenagers aged 12–17 and adults aged 18+. The emphasis is on participation, enjoyment and cultural exchange in a relaxed and inclusive setting, and no previous dance experience is necessary.

The workshops form part of Limerick’s county-pairing programme with Germany, celebrating the cultural connections between Ireland and Germany.

Name: Atlantic Breath: Anam Traidisiún ó Mhí go Galicia
Description:
Atlantic Breath: Anam Traidisiúin ó Mhí go Galicia brings the rich cultural traditions of Ireland and Galicia together for a special evening at Solstice Arts Centre in Navan.

Through music, song and dance, performers from Meath and Galicia explore the deep connections between these two Atlantic regions and celebrate their shared traditions and distinctive cultural identities.

Audiences can enjoy a lively programme showcasing traditional performance and collaboration, creating a cultural journey from Meath to north-west Spain. The event offers an opportunity to experience the rhythms, sounds and stories that connect communities across the Atlantic.

Readers are advised to check with the venue before relying on the details published here.
Address: Solstice Arts Centre, Railway St, Dillonsland, Navan, Meath

Name: EPIC x Jeanie Combo Ticket
Description:
Take a journey back in time, get an insight into life on board a Famine ship and hear the stories of the people who made the arduous voyage.

Then head into EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum to discover what happened to those who left, and the huge global impact they managed to have all over the world. 

Your experience begins at the Jeanie, and you’re free to explore EPIC at your own pace afterwards. The Jeanie is located two minutes from EPIC.

Tours occur between 10am and 3.30pm every 30 minutes - a guided Jeanie tour takes 50 minutes while visitors should leave themselves 90 minutes to explore EPIC.

Name: Irish Arts and Human Rights Festival 2026
Description:
Smashing Times and Front Line Defenders, and a range of partners, present the eighth annual Irish Arts and Human Rights Festival from 9 - 18 October 2026. The festival features exciting and innovative events that promote equality, human rights and diversity throughout Ireland, Northern Ireland and internationally.  

The aim of the festival is to showcase and highlight the extraordinary work of human rights defenders in Ireland and around the world, past and present, and the role of the arts and artists in promoting human rights today. The festival has sought to be as inclusive as possible; opening up to all artists across Ireland and internationally and to all communities including those experiencing marginalization and disadvantage.
Address: 30 Sandycove Road, Sandycove, Dublin

Name: Victorian Christmas Experience
Description:
This unique Christmas Experience brings children and their families on a guided festive adventure through 
Strokestown Park’s magnificent Palladian Mansion. 

Meet lots of lovable characters along the way who will give you a sneak peak behind the magic and entertain you from start to finish. The highlight of which will be a magical and wholesome visit with Santa who is waiting by the fire in the luxurious surrounding of Strokestown Park House Library.

Experience Includes: 
-Guided Theatrical Experience in a small group setting.
-Baking with Mrs Claus in our Galleried Kitchen.
-A visit to Santa’s Library to choose a book to take home.
-Elf Cobbler’s Traditional Woodland Games
-Arts & Crafts Activities 
-Hot Drink & Festive Treat

Name: Design Kenmare 2026
Description:
This autumn, the picturesque town of Kenmare will host the second annual Design Kenmare, a festival celebrating creativity and design across disciplines — from architecture and interiors to fashion, graphics, photography, and product design. Uniquely, the focus will be on understanding and experiencing design differently from other events. 

Taking place over three days, from November 13th – 15th, the festival will feature a world-class line-up of Irish and international designers, architects, photographers and creative thinkers in an intimate programme of talks and panels. Our festival celebrates design in all it's forms. 

Discover new perspectives. Connect with creative minds. Experience design differently.
Address: Kenmare, Kerry

Name: The Haunted Trail: Malahide Samhain Festival
Description:
Celebrate the Home of Halloween at The Haunted Trail: Malahide Samhain Festival! Journey through four immersive zones across the grounds of Malahide castle this October 17th-31st.

Encounter hidden characters on the interactive woodland trail including Puck, Malahide’s resident ghost, step back in time at the Celtic Samhain Village with ancient Irish traditions including turnip carving, live fire performances and hear eerie myths and music at the storytelling stage. Name: RTÉ CO Presents: A Little Fright Music
Description:
You might know it as Halloween, but the origins of this carnival of all things supernatural lie deep within our Celtic roots – traditions such as trick or treat, apple bobbing and jack o’lanterns were all part of Samhain, the pagan Harvest-time celebration of All Hallow’s Eve.
 
Join us in a musical celebration of this ancient Irish festival - and indulge our continuing love for all things ghoulish, ghostly and chilling of the spine. We’ll certainly put a spell on you, thanks to the RTE Concert Orchestra under the baton of our very own Fright Manager, Mister Guy “Beetlejuice” Barker, with voodoo vocals from “Killer Joe” Stilgoe and Naomi “Vampira” Banks.

Name: Apitherapy Seminar - Bee Products for Health & Wellbeing
Description:
The Tullamore Apitherapy Seminar on 14 November 2026 will offer both beekeepers and curious members of the public an insight into the variety of complementary ways bee products can be used in health and wellbeing.

Speaker Amadej Kastelic, a certified Slovenian apitherapist, will demonstrate the use of bee products such as honey, propolis, beeswax, pollen, royal jelly, and bee venom.

There is a strong practical aspect to the day with recipes for ointments, soap and tinctures. He will also discuss more unusual therapies including honey massage.

This event is hosted by Offaly Beekeepers Association and Lake County Beekeeper Association.

Name: Dara Molloy in Conversation with Tom Kenny
Description:
Join us with Celtic Monk and author Dara Molloy who will be in conversation with Tom Kenny about his new book, The Celtic Way.

Dara Molloy is an author and former Catholic priest turned Celtic monk who has lived on Inis Mór for more than forty years. He performs Celtic spiritual ceremonies, especially weddings, and is a guide to pilgrim groups visiting the island. The Celtic Way is a revelatory journey into Ireland’s ancient spiritual soul. The book blends memoir, myth and scholarship to illuminate a vibrant spiritual tradition rooted in nature, community and a worldview far broader than the Christianity that later overshadowed it.

Description:

Description:
From County Kerry, The O’Neill Sisters - three siblings singing in harmony - have captivated audiences across four continents, from Dublin’s National Concert Hall to Tokyo’s Orchard Hall. Name: Come Fly With Me: Aviation, Tourism and Irish Design
Description:
Our current exhibition at the National Print Museum, Come Fly With Me: Aviation, Tourism and Irish Design, uses flight as a central thread to explore how design and print helped promote Irish modernisation and position Ireland internationally. With the arrival of a number of Dutch graphic designers to Ireland in the 1950s to work on advertising for Aer Lingus, depictions of Ireland and Irishness were forever changed, as was Ireland’s relationship to Continental Europe and the US. Their design work was recognised internationally and had a huge impact on Irish design and economic development.

Free admission.

Address: National Print Museum, Haddington Rd, Dublin

Name: The Taylor Swift Tour
Description:
In 2024, ahead of Taylor’s sold-out Eras Tour, the Irish Family History Centre did some digging into the popstar’s genealogy. Turned out there was more to the singer’s love of Aran jumpers and the Irish druid aesthetic for her 2020 album Folklore than just preference – there’s Irish in her blood.

As a result of the research, a specialised themed tour for Swifties was created; the EPIC Museum, seen through a fresh lens, by uncovering the roots of one Miss Taylor Alison Swift, and her many connections to Ireland, whether it’s the inspiration behind one of her albums, her fashion sense, or her lyricism.

The Irish Family History Centre is available to assist visitors in their genealogy journey, based on-site at EPIC.

Name: The Pride Tour – Queer Irish, Global Impact
Description:
LGBTQ+ equality in Ireland only came relatively recently. Homosexuality was only decriminalised in 1993, with marriage equality following in 2015. However, LGBTQ+ people have always been part of Ireland’s story, and for many, emigration offered the chance to live more openly.

Our Pride Tour explores some of these stories, looking at the lives of LGBTQ+ Irish emigrants, activists, artists and other figures who challenged attitudes at home and made their mark around the world.

Based in Dublin's Docklands, EPIC tells the true story of the Irish, and acts as the base for the Irish Family History Centre. It also sits across from the Jeanie Johnston Famine Ship, just 2 minutes away.
Address: EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum, The Chq Building, Custom House Quay, North Wall, Dublin, Dublin

Name: Come Fly With Me: Aviation, Tourism and Irish Design
Description:
Our current exhibition at the National Print Museum, Come Fly With Me: Aviation, Tourism and Irish Design, uses flight as a central thread to explore how design and print helped promote Irish modernisation and position Ireland internationally. With the arrival of a number of Dutch graphic designers to Ireland in the 1950s to work on advertising for Aer Lingus, depictions of Ireland and Irishness were forever changed, as was Ireland’s relationship to Continental Europe and the US. Their design work was recognised internationally and had a huge impact on Irish design and economic development.

Free admission.

Name: The Origins of Halloween Tour
Description:
Learn more about The Dullahan (“dark man”) a malevolent harbinger of death who served as the inspiration for the headless horseman of Sleepy Hollow, or how the local practice of burying corpses with a stake through the heart influenced the writings of Irish emigrant Bram Stoker, author of Dracula.

Uncover the tragic story of ‘Goody Annie Glover’ the unfortunate Irish woman who became the last person hanged for witchcraft in Boston in 1688 and how the influx of Irish immigrants, who brought their traditions and folktales, helped shape the story of jack-o’-lanterns in America.

This ticket includes entry to EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum and a bespoke tour.

Adult tickets cost €24, teenager tickets cost €16.
Address: EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum, The Chq Building, Custom House Quay, North Wall, Dublin, Dublin

Description:

Name: Toil and Trouble ~ Cailleach by Macnas
Description:
Petronilla, burnt at the stake, now leads and controls the energies of fire through the streets of Kilkenny. She is accompanied by ecstatic townsfolk, marching behind her to the rhythm of their drums while Alice commands the scene from behind, giving life with the help of her mysterious healers.

Cailleach combines large-scale puppetry with incredible performances and special effects to create an image of Petronilla and Alice as influential women of their time, while reimagining the figure of the witch as a force shaping the stories around her.

Outdoor free event for all ages.

Part of Kilkenny's Toil & Trouble Festival

Name: Toil and Trouble ~ Cures and Curses by Sarah McKenna
Description:
For two years, Sarah documented traditional cures and curses from the border counties and she has a story to tell about where this ancient practice fits with modern Ireland. ‘The cure’, as it is known, is the ability of a unique person, place, or object to heal particular illnesses, while curses are deeply tied with dark folklore, invoking the land to betray it’s inhabitants.

An unusual tradition for a Western European country to have, surviving centuries of colonialisation, religious change, and famine, it connects us directly with our ancestors. Now it faces a future where they could be lost.

A storytelling performance intertwining Irish mythology with her journey collecting stories from people who practice an extraordinary tradition.

Description:
Play the enchanting Bemusement Games in the Rothe Courtyard and let DJ Raven's spooky tunes set the scene. Print a folklore and witches themed storybook page with artist Blaise Butler and follow the clues in a quest to discover the witch’s hidden treasure through Rothe House Gardens. Description:
Molly Aitken's novel, imagines Alice Kyteler from the inside: an innkeeper's daughter who took over her father's trade and grew it, built a fortune in a city that had no place for a wealthy woman, married four times and outlived three husbands, and found that the gossip trailing her money could harden, in the end, into a charge that carried a death sentence.

In this intimate reading and conversation in the Parade Tower at Kilkenny Castle, hosted by novelist Anya Bergman, Aitken brings medieval Kilkenny to life and opens up the questions underneath the story.

Hosted by Peter Dunne (Petrified Podcast)and featuring writers and performers from Kilkenny, with John Morton and Mairead Kiernan penning tales of terror and performers Amy Dunne and Ed Murphy bringing them to life.

Name: Toil and Trouble ~ Burning Woman
Description:
This new seminar, brings together historians, feminist voices and storytellers to dig into the Kilkenny Witch trial and the bigger themes hiding inside it – power, wealth, status, church and state, and who gets blamed, excluded or pushed to the margins. 

Joining the panel are Dr Andrew Sneddon, Senior Lecturer in International History at Ulster University and a leading historian of witchcraft and magic in Ireland; Dr Celeste McNamara, Assistant Professor in Early Modern European History at DCU; and Mary McAuliffe, Director of Gender Studies at UCD. 

Part history, part hard conversation, Burning Woman connects a 700-year-old trial to very present-day questions about power, gender and belonging.

Free, ticket required | Ages 16+

Name: Toil and Trouble ~ BRIDGET film screening + Q&A
Description:
The case became known internationally as the last witch burning in Ireland. She was buried at night, without mourners. 

Bridget is the first film by Anne Williamson, who grew up two townlands from where it happened, hearing the story at her grandfather's fireside. it sets a present-day framing in colour against a black-and-white retelling of Bridget's final days, shot by cinematographer Louis Buggy of Kilkenny's Diceman Films. It carries an original ballad, The Maid of Old Clooneen, written and sung by Chris Kavanagh. 
The screening is followed by a Q&A with Anne Williamson.

Name: Toil and Trouble ~ Anakronos presents The Red Book of Ossory
Description:
In 1324, the Bishop Richard de Ledrede, accused Dame Alice Kyteler of witchcraft. Her maid, Petronilla de Meath, was burned at the stake that November.

Ledrede also wrote poetry: Latin poems, gathered in a fourteenth-century manuscript known as the Red Book of Ossory. Led by founder member of ANÚNA, Caitríona O'Leary, Anakronos have set these poems to music influenced by contemporary classical, jazz and medieval music to create a brand new sound. They perform them St. Canice's Cathedral, where Ledrede was bishop. 

Part of Kilkenny's Toil & Trouble Festival

Internationally renowned composer Matthew Nolan, accompanied by musicians Seán Mac Erlaine, Lisa Dowdall and Kilkenny native Damien Lennon, present a specially-commissioned live score for Nietzchka Keene’s stark, stunning debut feature The Juniper Tree.

Name: Rebels and Revolutionaries | Women’s History Tour
Description:
The Rebels and Revolutionaries Women’s History Tour focuses on the ones who broke out of societal shackles to make an impact around the world. Today, we are thankfully very familiar with some of these women. The likes of Mary Robinson, Ireland’s first female president, and Countess Markievicz, an instrumental figure in the 1916 Easter Rising, are well known. But many others have been largely lost to history, despite their impressive achievements.

This tour draws attention to those left out of the history books, exploring how women’s stories have been hidden for many years and how, in modern times, historians have been revisiting, rediscovering and revealing these crucial pieces of the puzzle.
Address: EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum, The Chq Building, Custom House Quay, North Wall, Dublin, Dublin

Name: The CHQ Tour | One of Dublin’s Iconic Buildings
Description:
This is a rare opportunity to explore the rich heritage of the Docklands area and uncover the unique story behind the building, its architecture, and its role in shaping the city. The CHQ Building, originally known as Stack A, was constructed in the early 19th century as part of the broader Custom House docks complex. This tour offers the chance to step back in time and discover the building’s original purpose as a bonded warehouse for storing valuable cargo including tobacco, tea, wine and spirits.

On the CHQ tour, you’ll also hear the fascinating story of its transformation into a grand Banqueting Hall in 1856, when thousands gathered for an enormous celebration in honour of Irish soldiers returning from the Crimean War.
Address: EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum, The Chq Building, Custom House Quay, North Wall, Dublin, Dublin

Name: The Pride Tour – Queer Irish, Global Impact
Description:
LGBTQ+ equality in Ireland only came relatively recently. Homosexuality was only decriminalised in 1993, with marriage equality following in 2015. However, LGBTQ+ people have always been part of Ireland’s story, and for many, emigration offered the chance to live more openly.

Our Pride Tour explores some of these stories, looking at the lives of LGBTQ+ Irish emigrants, activists, artists and other figures who challenged attitudes at home and made their mark around the world.

Based in Dublin's Docklands, EPIC tells the true story of the Irish, and acts as the base for the Irish Family History Centre. It also sits across from the Jeanie Johnston Famine Ship, just 2 minutes away.
Address: EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum, The Chq Building, Custom House Quay, North Wall, Dublin, Dublin

Name: AN 424: AN BUS GO DTÍ AN GHEALCHATHAIR | THE BUS TO THE BRIGHTCITY
Description:
Tar linn ar aistear draíochta an 424, an bus a thógann muid ó dhorchadas na maidine thiar i gCarna tríd bhóithre casta Chonamara go dtí an Ghealchathair. Fág ‘aiteann, fraoch, fiataíl, srutháin, claíocha, tolláin, gleannta’ i do dhiaidh agus tú ar oilithreacht i dtreo na Gaillimhe.

Everyone who lives in Conamara or who has visited knows the road the 424 bus takes west from Galway city, along the coast, past lakes, bogs and hills to quiet fields where men and cattle stop to gaze at the colourful bus.

With music from Trá Pháidín, whose first album was An 424, and visuals from broadcaster and film maker Donal Dineen. Curated by Majella Ní Chríocháin.

Name: CRANN MÓR | TREE
Description:
Tá Nick Roth tar éis an leagan Gaeilge de a rinne Gabriel Rosenstock a chur in oiriúint do chór guthanna leis na hamhránaithe Caitríona O’Leary, Michelle O’Rourke agus Olesya Zdorovetska.

Richard Berengarten’s poem Tree is a symphonic hymn to a tree in all its aspects, drawing on its sacred and central place in the world’s mythology, history and religion. Commissioned by IMRAM in 2020, Gabriel Rosenstock’s Irish language translation of the poem Crann was first presented as a film directed by Laura Hilliard. 

This expanded version of Crann Mór for nine voices, percussion and film sees the upper voices of Chamber Choir Ireland and conductor David Young join the original vocal trio in a new live staging, directed by Adrian Dunbar.
Address: Smock Alley Theatre, 1662, 6-7 Exchange Street Lower, Temple Bar, Dublin, Dublin

Name: 'Thinning the Veil': Art Exhibition
Description:
Six contemporary Fingal artists come together at Malahide Castle this autumn in an exhibition exploring memory, history, heritage and the changing role of monuments in contemporary Ireland. Curated by Eamonn Maxwell, the exhibition features sculptures, installations, sound works and graphic pieces throughout the castle.

From 22 September, the programme continues with free special events including a Curator’s Tour & Artist Q&A with Eamonn Maxwell and Deborah Hewson, artist talks and exhibition tours with Ann Ensor, Laura Skehan, Michelle Hall and Susan Buttner, a live performance by Tadhg Kinsella, and a closing night exhibition tour with Cathal Dowd Smith. Advance booking is required for events.
Address: Malahide Castle & Gardens, Back Rd, Malahide Demesne, Malahide, Dublin

Name: DIAMAINT AGUS MEIRG | DIAMONDS AND RUST: THE DYLAN-BAEZ PROJECT
Description:
IMRAM has already staged two hugely successful Bob Dylan projects – one on his greatest hits, and the other on his gospel songs. This new project focuses on his creative and personal relationship with Joan Baez.

Name: The CHQ Tour | One of Dublin’s Iconic Buildings
Description:
This is a rare opportunity to explore the rich heritage of the Docklands area and uncover the unique story behind the building, its architecture, and its role in shaping the city. The CHQ Building, originally known as Stack A, was constructed in the early 19th century as part of the broader Custom House docks complex. This tour offers the chance to step back in time and discover the building’s original purpose as a bonded warehouse for storing valuable cargo including tobacco, tea, wine and spirits.

On the CHQ tour, you’ll also hear the fascinating story of its transformation into a grand Banqueting Hall in 1856, when thousands gathered for an enormous celebration in honour of Irish soldiers returning from the Crimean War.
Address: EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum, The Chq Building, Custom House Quay, North Wall, Dublin, Dublin

Name: Sarah Long: Residency & Exhibition
Description:
Sarah Long is an artist based in Cork. She creates autofiction that she translates across painting, performance and publication. Sarah identifies reverberations in Irish culture and combines these references with personal stories and motifs. 

During this exhibition and residency in Triskel Sample Project Space, Sarah takes up the position of the girl or girlishness, to obfuscate archetypes such as woman or mother. Through her character Mary, Sarah engages in an autofictionalised approach. She will develop a new body of autofictional writing into a new performance. The work plays with the notion of the aisling, an Irish poetic genre where the nation appears to the poet in a dream in the form of a woman.
Address: Triskel Arts Centre, Tobin St, Centre, Cork

During this exhibition and residency in Triskel Sample Project Space, Sarah takes up the position of the girl or girlishness, to obfuscate archetypes such as woman or mother. Through her character Mary, Sarah engages in an autofictionalised approach. She will develop a new body of autofictional writing into a new performance. The work plays with the notion of the aisling, an Irish poetic genre where the nation appears to the poet in a dream in the form of a woman.
Address: Triskel Arts Centre, Tobin St, Centre, Cork

Name: It's A Wonderful Life
Description:
The play follows the life of George Bailey, a man with big dreams of travelling the world and building skyscrapers, who instead finds himself rooted in his hometown by duty and heart. On a fateful, snowy Christmas Eve, facing financial ruin and despair, George contemplates the unthinkable. It is then that he meets Clarissa Oddbody, an “Angel Second Class” who has been waiting over two hundred years to earn her wings. 

It’s a Wonderful Life is a story of hope, redemption, and the reminder that every time a bell rings, an angel gets its wings. 

21 Nov - 10 Jan 2027

“Never thinks about himself, God. That’s why he’s in trouble. He needs a Guardian Angel.”

Readers are advised to check with the venue before relying on the details published here.

Name: 75th Wexford Festival Opera
Description:
17 Days | 75 Events | 75 Years of Extraordinary

From its origins in 1951 to what is now a world-renowned opera festival, Wexford has always been about vision. 

Running from 15-31 October, the 75th Anniversary season offers not only an opportunity to look back on a legacy of rediscovery and artistic courage, but to experience it anew.

This year's Festival brings together a rich programme of rediscoveries, world premieres and unforgettable performances from Ermonela Jaho, Joseph Calleja, Daniella Barcellona and many more stars. From our three mainstage operas to the special Croí na Féile (Heart of the Festival) Fundraising Gala Concert, explore the programme and join opera-lovers from all over the world in Wexford this October.
Address: National Opera House, High St, Townparks, Wexford

Name: Féile na Bealtaine 2027
Description:
Féile na Bealtaine which takes place annually on the Dingle peninsula since 1994 has established itself as a top-ranking voluntary community arts festival – a reliably high standard, energetic, open festival, welcoming to all that have sympathies with the area, and an artistic home to dozens of local performing artists. The festival invites contributors to push boundaries, exploring new venues, experiments with form and collaborate, while remaining true to the festival’s deep roots in a rural community.

Readers are advised to check with the organiser before relying on the details published here.
Address: Dingle Peninsula, Kerry

Name: Siobhán Collins: Residency & Exhibition
Description:
Siobhán is a visual artist living in Cork City. She works across several mediums, including pencil, charcoal, watercolour and oils. Her work foregrounds play, materiality and embodiment. Her drawings and paintings are primarily figurative and explorative.

During her time in Triskel Sample Project Space, Siobhán will do a practice-based research residency in contemporary portraiture. She will engage the public by drawing and painting the faces of people living in Cork. She will create approximately 40 portraits over the course of 4 weeks, make space for critical reflection, and partake in an artist talk during her solo exhibition.

The portrait studies will vary in duration from 15 minutes to 2 hours.
Address: Triskel Arts Centre, Tobin St, Centre, Cork

Name: Kilrush Genealogy Conference 2026: From the Great Famine to the 1926 Census
Description:
18 April 2026 was a landmark date in Irish genealogy with the release of the 1926 Census of the Irish Free State, the first comprehensive snapshot of Ireland after independence, which sparked a major surge in genealogical research. 

To mark this historic event, Kilrush & District Historical Society will host the Kilrush Genealogy Conference 2026: From the Great Famine to the 1926 Census, featuring a distinguished line-up of speakers.

Experienced genealogists will also provide one-to-one consultations for attendees. Add-ons include a Loop Head bus tour, a visit to Scattery Island, and a conference dinner. Free events include a historical walking tour of Kilrush and a traditional music seisiún. 

Anyone with Irish ancestors is welcome.
Address: Kilrush, Clare

Name: Iarla Ó Lionáird with Cormac McCarthy & Caoimhín Ó Raghallaigh
Description:
Promising to be a very memorable and unique concert, this is an inspired pairing of twice Grammy nominated vocalist Iarla Ó Lionáird with renowned pianist/composer Cormac McCarthy and acclaimed fiddle maestro Caoimhín Ó Raghallaigh.

Iarla Ó Lionáird has carved a long and unique career in music both internationally and in Ireland.

From his iconic early recording of the vision song “Aisling Gheal” as a young boy to his ground breaking recordings with Dublin’s Crash Ensemble and New York’s Alarm Will Sound, he has shown a breadth of artistic ambition that sets him apart in the Irish Music fraternity.

Name: Siobhán Collins: Residency & Exhibition
Description:
Siobhán is a visual artist living in Cork City. She works across several mediums, including pencil, charcoal, watercolour and oils. Her work foregrounds play, materiality and embodiment. Her drawings and paintings are primarily figurative and explorative.

During her time in Triskel Sample Project Space, Siobhán will do a practice-based research residency in contemporary portraiture. She will engage the public by drawing and painting the faces of people living in Cork. She will create approximately 40 portraits over the course of 4 weeks, make space for critical reflection, and partake in an artist talk during her solo exhibition.

The portrait studies will vary in duration from 15 minutes to 2 hours.
Address: Triskel Arts Centre, Tobin St, Centre, Cork

Name: Dublin Port Behind-the-scenes Bus Tours
Description:
Visit  the heart of a working port and gain insight into how Dublin stays connected to the world. This guided bus tour takes you into operational areas not normally accessible to the public, including container terminals, ferry berths and key industrial zones. 

Handling €165 billion in trade and 1.6 million passengers annually, Dublin Port is central to the national economy. The tour also explores its ongoing transformation under the Masterplan 2040, alongside its industrial heritage and evolving relationship with the city.

Tours last approximately 2 hours and run from April to October on Wednesdays & Saturdays. 
Advance booking is essential.

Readers are advised to check with the organiser before relying on the details published here.
Venue Name: Meeting Point: EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum
Address: EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum, The Chq Building, Custom House Quay, North Wall, Dublin, Dublin

Name: Friday Night Supper Club
Description:
This is quite a unique night! We think that it’s a great tradition to make at least one Friday night a month a delectable social affair full of good music, good drinks, and fantastic food. On arrival you can expect to be fortified with a glass of your favourite tipple followed by a lively demonstration where we will run through a couple of elements from the evening’s menu. 

Enjoy a hands-on session where you will get involved in some cooking (generally the starter and dessert), before being seated in the dining room to savour delicious food and company restaurant-style. The supper clubs are highly suitable for both groups as well as those flying solo.

Readers are advised to check with the venue before relying on the details published here.
Address: 2 Brookfield Terrace, Blackrock, Dublin

Name: Galway Céilí Club - Beginners Class
Description:
No experience? No problem! The Galway Céilí Club is dedicated to making traditional Irish dance accessible and fun for all. With expert guidance, you’ll learn the basics of céilí dancing, Irish set dances, and even European folk dances. It’s not just a class; it’s an exhilarating workout wrapped in music and camaraderie.

The club was born from a passion for bringing céilí dancing out of the shadows and into the heart of Galway’s vibrant social scene. And they’ve succeeded. Locals and visitors alike rave about the energy, connection, and sheer fun these evenings provide.

Whether you’re visiting Galway for the first time or are a long-time resident, this is your chance to immerse yourself in a quintessentially Irish tradition.
Address: Kennedys, 47 Eyre Square, Galway
