Celebrating its 10th anniversary in 2026, the award winning Mayo Dark Sky Festival invites visitors to the welcoming communities of Newport, Mulranny and Ballycroy, set within one of Ireland’s most pristine dark sky regions along the Wild Atlantic Way. 

This special edition features an exciting programme of guided stargazing, expert talks, astrophotography workshops, seashore safaris and family-friendly events. By day, explore the area’s stunning landscapes and rich heritage; by night, experience breathtaking nightscapes, haunting musical performances and the iconic Lantern Walk finale. 

Readers are advised to check with the organiser before relying on the details published here.
Address: Hotel Newport, Main St, Newport, Mayo

Name: Irish Mythology Storytelling Experience
Description:
Step into the darker, more powerful world of Irish mythology through this live storytelling performance. Performed entirely from memory, this intimate one-man theatrical show brings Ireland’s legendary heroes, warriors and ancient tales to vivid life. 

Audiences experience stories of heroism, passion, violence and fate as they were originally told long before they were softened for modern audiences. Designed for mature audiences, this is a unique cultural experience that offers visitors a deeper, more memorable encounter with Irish mythology and storytelling tradition.

Readers are advised to check with the organiser before relying on the details published here.
Address: 14 Ormond Quay Upper, North City, Dublin

Name: Féile Sheáin Mhic Pháidín - John McFadden Festival
Description:
Immerse yourself in the magic of Féile Sheáin Mhic Pháidín, Newport’s celebration of traditional music and heritage. Honouring the legacy of 19th-century fiddler John McFadden, the festival transforms the heart of Mayo into a lively hub of rhythm and culture. 

The weekend features masterclasses in music, song and dance, alongside performances from some of the finest traditional musicians. Enjoy the Céilí, the intimate concert, the Cuimsiú Session, the cosy Rambling House, Comhrá Gaeilge and so much more. Whether you're a festival regular or a first-timer, a warm welcome and friendly atmosphere await. Set against the beautiful backdrop of Clew Bay, it’s the perfect place to enjoy the unique spirit and culture of Newport in the West of Ireland
Address: Newport, Mayo

Name: Enya Martin - Acting the Divil
Description:
Acting the Divil explores the funny side of modern fitness culture, the quiet truth of a long-term, childless relationship.

Enya Martin reflects on growing up in the 90s on a council estate, to eventually flying first class to Australia. She explores the many hurdles she’s come up against in life that has shaped her into the comedian she is today, and her mother is still the punch line to most of her jokes!  

A funny, heartfelt hour about chasing success while staying true to the people who shaped you.

Name: Sarah Long: Residency & Exhibition
Description:
Sarah Long is an artist based in Cork. She creates autofiction that she translates across painting, performance and publication. Sarah identifies reverberations in Irish culture and combines these references with personal stories and motifs. 

During this exhibition and residency in Triskel Sample Project Space, Sarah takes up the position of the girl or girlishness, to obfuscate archetypes such as woman or mother. Through her character Mary, Sarah engages in an autofictionalised approach. She will develop a new body of autofictional writing into a new performance. The work plays with the notion of the aisling, an Irish poetic genre where the nation appears to the poet in a dream in the form of a woman.
Address: Triskel Arts Centre, Tobin St, Centre, Cork

Name: The Cable
Description:
Set on Valentia Island in 1866 during the laying of the Transatlantic Cable — known as the “Eighth Wonder of the World” — the play unfolds as a poignant story of love, loss, and the enduring human need for connection in a world on the brink of a communications revolution. Featuring a haunting score of Irish music by Dave McGilton, The Cable combines rich storytelling with emotional depth and theatrical intensity. Rooted in Irish heritage and brought to life through Siamsa Tíre’s distinctive theatrical style, this is a powerful and immersive production. 

The Cable promises an unforgettable evening of drama as it tours stages at home and abroad. Don’t miss this unforgettable theatrical event where history, heart, and heritage meet on stage.
Address: Backstage Theatre, Farneyhoogan, Farranyoogan, Longford

Name: The Bartered Bride
Description:
One bride. Two suitors.

Set in a busy Czech village bound by tradition and tangled in secrets, The Bartered Bride is a fast-paced comic opera where two young lovers attempt to rewrite the rules. To be together, they need to outwit a meddling matchmaker, sidestep an unwanted marriage contract and survive the arrival of a traveling circus.

At the heart of the story is Irish soprano Amy Ní Fhearraigh as Mařenka, a spirited young woman determined to marry for love but promised to a wealthy landowner’s son. Russian-Ukrainian tenor Egor Zhuravskii sings her devoted, but not entirely honest lover, Jeník.

Smetana’s melodic score bursts with infectious folk rhythms, dazzling duets and the vibrant energy of its famous overture and dances.
Address: Backstage Theatre, Farneyhoogan, Farranyoogan, Longford

Name: Rob Luft & Elina Duni - Reaching For The Moon
Description:
In 2017, Elina Duni and Rob Luft’s paths crossed at the Montreux Jazz Festival, marking the inception of a unique project. Their upcoming 2026 album, a stripped-back duo effort, revisits the essence of their initial meeting.

Here we can witness the stark beauty of Elina Duni’s vocals blending with Rob Luft’s crystalline guitar lines in a mesmerizing dance. Together, they weave a tapestry of songs that evoke the mystery and joy of the night, the moon, and the magic that lives within us all. This musical journey is a gentle caress, a soothing lullaby that offers hope in the darkness, reminding us of the solace of home.

Elina Duni – Vocals & Percussion
Rob Luft – Guitar & Electronics

Part of Triskel International Jazz Programme 2026.
Address: Triskel Arts Centre, Tobin St, Centre, Cork

Name: Pints, Dentures & Rock ’n’ Roll
Description:
This time the characters aren’t just having the craic … they’re fully out of control.

Expect a fast-paced, laugh-out-loud night of rural Irish chaos as Tadhg brings an entire parish of walking disasters to life.

From fed-up farmers and drunken plumbers to failed musicians and an undertaker obsessed with recycling the dead, nothing in this village is normal — but who likes normal!?

Name: Galway Céilí Club - Beginners Class
Description:
No experience? No problem! The Galway Céilí Club is dedicated to making traditional Irish dance accessible and fun for all. With expert guidance, you’ll learn the basics of céilí dancing, Irish set dances, and even European folk dances. It’s not just a class; it’s an exhilarating workout wrapped in music and camaraderie.

The club was born from a passion for bringing céilí dancing out of the shadows and into the heart of Galway’s vibrant social scene. And they’ve succeeded. Locals and visitors alike rave about the energy, connection, and sheer fun these evenings provide.

Whether you’re visiting Galway for the first time or are a long-time resident, this is your chance to immerse yourself in a quintessentially Irish tradition.
Address: Kennedys, 47 Eyre Square, Galway

Name: Dublin By Dusk at EPIC Museum
Description:
On the last Thursday of each month until November, EPIC will remain open until 9pm, with tickets available for just €10 and a special evening guided tour (for €15) with limited availability.

Evening museum visits offer a quieter, more relaxed way to experience Dublin's cultural attractions. Visitors can explore at their own pace after work, avoid daytime crowds, and enjoy a different atmosphere in the city's historic Docklands.

A museum as tailored for locals as it is for tourists, if you've never visited EPIC, let this be your sign. Discover Ireland's long emigration history, and the global influence of the diaspora in this fully immersive and interactive museum.
Address: EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum, The Chq Building, Custom House Quay, North Wall, Dublin, Dublin

Name: EPIC Exhibition - Common Ground: Ireland in the EU
Description:
Ireland joined the European Economic Community (EEC) – as the EU was then known – on January 1, 1973, after a referendum endorsed by 83% of voters. It was then among the poorest and most underdeveloped countries in western Europe, with a population just over half of its current size.

Ireland’s accession proved to be the most consequential economic milestone in the half century since Irish independence, but it also set in motion far-reaching social and cultural change. EU legislation has driven improvements in workers’ rights, for example, and set binding targets for climate action. Irish people have studied and built new lives across Europe, while many Europeans have since made their homes here in Ireland.
Address: EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum, The Chq Building, Custom House Quay, North Wall, Dublin, Dublin

Ireland’s accession proved to be the most consequential economic milestone in the half century since Irish independence, but it also set in motion far-reaching social and cultural change. EU legislation has driven improvements in workers’ rights, for example, and set binding targets for climate action. Irish people have studied and built new lives across Europe, while many Europeans have since made their homes here in Ireland.

Ireland joined the European Economic Community (EEC) – as the EU was then known – on January 1, 1973, after a referendum endorsed by 83% of voters. It was then among the poorest and most underdeveloped countries in western Europe, with a population just over half of its current size.

Ireland’s accession proved to be the most consequential economic milestone in the half century since Irish independence, but it also set in motion far-reaching social and cultural change. EU legislation has driven improvements in workers’ rights, for example, and set binding targets for climate action. Irish people have studied and built new lives across Europe, while many Europeans have since made their homes here in Ireland.
Address: EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum, The Chq Building, Custom House Quay, North Wall, Dublin, Dublin

Ireland’s accession proved to be the most consequential economic milestone in the half century since Irish independence, but it also set in motion far-reaching social and cultural change. EU legislation has driven improvements in workers’ rights, for example, and set binding targets for climate action. Irish people have studied and built new lives across Europe, while many Europeans have since made their homes here in Ireland.
Address: EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum, The Chq Building, Custom House Quay, North Wall, Dublin, Dublin

Name: Dingle Literary Festival 2026
Description:
Set against the dramatic beauty of Ireland’s Atlantic coast, the Dingle Literary Festival is a celebration of storytelling in all its forms. Across an inspiring weekend in the heart of Dingle, acclaimed authors, emerging voices, poets, musicians and readers come together for conversations, readings, performances and debate. 

From intimate discussions and lively panels to late-night music sessions and seaside encounters, the festival captures the creativity, warmth and imagination that define the west of Ireland. Whether you come for the books, the atmosphere, or the chance to connect with writers and fellow readers, the Dingle Lit offers a rich and memorable cultural experience in one of Ireland’s most captivating towns.
Address: An Diseart, Green St, Farrannakilla, Dingle, Kerry

Name: Westport Sea 2 Summit Adventure Race
Description:
Two separate races with three categories in both, which will include a mix of road running, cycling, and a mountain hike.

The Sea2Summit Spirit caters for the participant that wants a challenge but has not taken part in adventure racing before. Duration time for the fastest will be 2.5 – 3hrs.

The Sea2Summit Supreme is for the participant who wants an extra challenge. The hike up and down the front face of Croagh Patrick (Murrisk) will hurt the legs and the back breaking ramps at the Maum climb will definitely test your bike and quad muscles.
Duration time for the elite athletes will be around 3.5hrs.

In these two races, there are 3 categories to choose from:
Advanced | Intermediate | Beginner
Address: Carrowbeg, Westport, Mayo

Name: Declan O'Rourke: Oceanic
Description:
Declan O’Rourke brings Oceanic to the Gleneagle Club, Killarney on Saturday 7th November 2026.

 This special live performance promises an intimate and atmospheric evening, with rich storytelling, soaring vocals, and beautifully crafted arrangements that have made him one of Ireland’s most respected songwriters. 

Expect a blend of brand-new material from Oceanic alongside reimagined favourites from across his career, all performed in a warm, close-up setting that enhances every lyric and melody.

Tickets from €42.20. Doors 7.30pm, show 8.30pm.

Note: under 18s must be accompanied by an adult
Address: Gleneagle Killarney, Muckross Rd, Poulnamuck, Killarney, Kerry

Name: Cork International Choral Festival
Description:
Founded in 1954, the Cork International Choral Festival is one of Europe’s premier international choral festivals. It is held annually over the five days preceding the first Monday in May in venues across the city, centring around Cork City Hall, one of the most attractive and acoustically superb venues in Ireland. Overall, the Festival attracts some 5,000 participants and 50,000 people who bring Cork to life with song over the 5 days. It is noted for its diverse programme, high competitive standards, and the friendliness of its welcome. Highlights include:

	Superb Gala Concerts 
	Fringe Concerts | Free performances in popular tourist venues
	Fleischmann International Trophy Competition 
	Workshops & Masterclasses | Free events
Address: Cork City, Cork

Name: Wexford Light Opera Society presents 30th Anniversary Hits from the Musicals 2026
Description:
This milestone anniversary production will feature a carefully chosen repertoire of beloved Broadway and West End favourites, alongside contemporary musical theatre showstoppers, performed by the award-winning WLOS chorus, joined by some of the society’s most celebrated performers in an exciting cabaret style evening.

Under the expert musical direction of David Hayes, with stage direction by Stephen Byrne and choral direction by Eithne Corrigan, the production promises to capture the creativity and energy that have made Hits from the Musicals such a firm favourite with audiences for three decades.

Hosting the evening once again is the ever-charismatic Catherine “Biddy” Walsh.
Address: Whites of Wexford, Abbey St, Townparks, Wexford

Name: Phil Coulter ‘Gold and Silver Days’
Description:
In recent years Phil Coulter’s annual national tour has become, for his legion of fans, a hugely popular and welcome relief from the cold of the Irish winter. His 2026 tour promises to be a heart-warming trip down memory lane, as Phil takes his audience through some of the highlights of his glittering 60 year career.

Fans will relax in the glow of nostalgia as they hear piano favourites from his tranquillity series alongside his classic songs, from “Puppet on a String” to Elvis Presley, from “Scorn not his Simplicity” to the Bay City Rollers.

They will feel the power of “The Town I Loved So Well” and sing along with “Ireland’s Call”. An evening of pure quality, not to be missed!

Description:

Name: The Cable live at Siamsa Tíre
Description:
Siamsa Tíre is thrilled to welcome Aidan Dooley, renowned for the award-winning Tom Crean: Antarctic Explorer, as he directs Mike Kelly’s The Cable in a powerful new telling, co-produced by Siamsa Tíre.

Set against the backdrop of the Transatlantic Cable being laid on Valentia Island, this poignant story explores loss, hope, and the longing for connection. With a haunting score of stunning Irish music, The Cable is a tale of love, family, and the transformative power of communication.

Name: Stories from the Sea with Underwater Cameraman Ken O’Sullivan
Description:
Ken O’Sullivan, underwater cameraman and multiple-award winning film maker brings us on his 25 year journey exploring the North Atlantic ocean and seas around Ireland with an entirely new show, STORIES FROM THE SEA. 

From being surrounded by a pod of Killer whales to swimming with thousands of dolphins and the largest animals ever to have lived, Ken regales us with stories of the beauty of the natural world and our emotional connection with it and our ancient maritime culture in Ireland.

Tickets: General €22, Concession €20, Family(4) €75 +bf
Suitability: 7yrs+

Name: Rachel Grace
Description:
Drawing influence from modern pop and classic soul, Rachel’s sound is defined by its honesty and warmth. Her influences span soul, folk, and pop, with emotion and authenticity at the heart of everything she creates. With a voice that moves effortlessly from intimate and delicate to powerful and commanding, she brings a distinctive depth to every performance. Known for her intimate and engaging live performances, she has supported the likes of Gavin James, Roisin O, Jack L and Wallis Bird and has worked as a session musician for Roisin O and Irish Women In Harmony. 

This upcoming performance offers a chance to experience her sound up close—an evening of soulful melodies, honest storytelling, and undeniable talent.
Address: National Opera House, High St, Townparks, Wexford

Name: Solve-Along-A-Murder-She-Wrote
Description:
Cult hit event Solve-Along-A-Murder-She-Wrote returns to Wexford with an interactive screening of the classic Murder, She Wrote episode “Paint Me a Murder”. Jessica Fletcher visits an artist friend on a remote island hideaway, but soon there’s a murder that only JF (or you!) can solve!

Solve-Along-A-Murder-She-Wrote is a unique and hilarious night featuring games, prizes and audience participation, with special permission from NBC Universal Television. Hosted by super-fan Tim Benzie, Solve-Along-A-Murder-She-Wrote features:
* A race to solve to the crime, via the Fameometer and the Suspiciometer!
* A Cabot Cove quiz!
* A singalong to the theme tune with new lyrics!
* Clips and biogs of the campy guest stars!
Address: National Opera House, High St, Townparks, Wexford

Name: Dingle Literary Festival 2026
Description:
Set against the dramatic beauty of Ireland’s Atlantic coast, the Dingle Literary Festival is a celebration of storytelling in all its forms. Across an inspiring weekend in the heart of Dingle, acclaimed authors, emerging voices, poets, musicians and readers come together for conversations, readings, performances and debate. 

From intimate discussions and lively panels to late-night music sessions and seaside encounters, the festival captures the creativity, warmth and imagination that define the west of Ireland. Whether you come for the books, the atmosphere, or the chance to connect with writers and fellow readers, the Dingle Lit offers a rich and memorable cultural experience in one of Ireland’s most captivating towns.
Address: An Diseart, Green St, Farrannakilla, Dingle, Kerry

Name: Artist-Initiated Projects 2026
Description:
Between January–December 2026 we will present 8 x 3-week exhibitions of new work by:

Paddy Critchley, Fiona Marron, Finn Nichol, Emma Brennan and Thomas Wells, Ciara Rodgers, Struàn Bell, Christopher Mahon, neonatus.exe

Artist-Initiated Projects at Pallas Projects/Studios is an open-submission, annual gallery programme of 8 x 3-week exhibitions taking place between January and December 2026. This unique programme of funded, artist-initiated projects selected via open call is highly accessible to artists, with a focus on early career, emerging artists and recent graduates. Projects are supplemented with artists' talks, texts, workshops or performances, and gallery visits by colleges and local schools.
Address: Pallas Projects/Studios, 115-116, The Coombe, The Liberties, Dublin

Name: James Joyce Walking Tour
Description:
A fun and exciting walking tour of James Joyce's Dublin offered by the James Joyce Centre.

Though Joyce lived most of his life outside of Ireland, Dublin would provide the backdrop for virtually all of his work. On a stroll around the inner city, our guide will explain the real-life inspiration behind some of Joyce’s most celebrated writing, demonstrating just how central the streetscape of the ‘Hibernian metropolis’ was to the author’s life and art. The tour visits such stops as Belvedere College, the Gresham Hotel, the James Joyce Statue, Davy Byrnes, and the National Library.

This is an excellent and fun introduction to Joyce in a bustling part of the city.

Every Thur, Fri & Sat at 11am. Admission to the James Joyce Centre is included.
Address: James Joyce Centre, James Joyce House, 35 N Great George's St, Rotunda, Basement, Dublin

Name: Cork Comic Con 2026
Description:
Cork Comic Con is a major celebration of comics, pop culture and creative storytelling in the south of Ireland. The event brings together fans, families, artists and special guests from film, TV, animation and comics for a fun, welcoming weekend in Cork. Visitors can enjoy panels, Q&As, autograph sessions, cosplay showcases and interactive workshops in drawing, writing, costume design and SFX make-up. Artist Alley highlights Irish and international creators, while portfolio reviews and talks support emerging talent. 

With family-friendly activities and a lively atmosphere, Cork Comic Con offers a unique cultural experience celebrating imagination, creativity and community.
Address: Marina Market, Centre Park Rd, Ballintemple, Cork

Name: Trygve Seim & Tord Gustavsen: Inner Chorals
Description:
Two of the most striking lyrical ‘voices’ on the blooming Norwegian jazz scene and ECM Recording artists get together to play J. S. Bach . Trygve and Tord develop unique musical spaces of glowing stillness, lyrical beauty, and far-reaching expressivity while taking chorals written by – or attributed to – Bach as their point of departure.

The concert uses pieces like “Jesu, meine Freude”, “Auf meinen lieben Gott” and “Befiel du deine Wege”, and treats them with equal amounts of respect and freedom. The Programme will also include compositions by both artists, and perhaps some arrangements of Irish traditional tunes and compositions.

Supported by The River Lee, a Doyle Collection hotel.
Part of Triskel International Jazz Programme 2026.
Address: Triskel Arts Centre, Tobin St, Centre, Cork

Name: Live Aid Exhibition
Description:
Through a series of striking displays, the exhibition brings audiences on a visual journey of the Live Aid concerts, capturing the behind-the-scenes preparations, atmosphere and iconic performances by bands and artists on both sides of the Atlantic as the day unfolded.

From Status Quo, U2 and David Bowie in London, to Black Sabbath and Run DMC in Philadelphia Live Aid at the National Library of Ireland immerses visitors in the scale and spirit of this iconic event from the intimacy of the National Photographic Archive.

This free exhibition opens to the public daily (10.00am – 4.00pm)

Readers are advised to check with the organiser before relying on the details published here.
Address: National Photographic Archive, Meeting House Square, Temple Bar, Dublin

Name: The Dead by James Joyce
Description:
Following two completely sold-out runs, The Dead by James Joyce, a thrilling immersive theatre experience, returns by popular demand to Museum of Literature Ireland from 20 November 2026 - 31 January 2027.

The sell-out sensation The Dead, adapted and directed by Louise Lowe, is currently running from 21 Nov 2025 - 1 Feb 2026. 

This unforgettable production of Joyce's masterpiece takes place in the rich historical interior and unseen rooms of UCD Newman House. 

Audiences are greeted by the maid Lily – who is literally run off her feet – before taking the journey up the opulent staircase, to embark on an evening of laughter, music and dance – ending in an epiphany like no other.

Produced by ANU and Landmark Productions, in association with MoLI.
Venue Name: UCD Newman House, 85 St Stephen's Green
Address: 85 St Stephen's Green, Saint Kevin's, Dublin

Winterval 2026 will bring a mix of free and ticketed events including:

Winterval Illuminates: A signature 3D light projection show, often located at Cathedral Square.

Christmas Markets: Artisan stalls featuring local crafts and food, primarily centered in the Waterford Cultural Quarter.

Ice Skating: The "Waterford on Ice" rink is a staple feature located on the city's quayside.

Santa Experiences: Immersive meet-and-greets, historically held in unique venues like the Medieval Museum.

Name: Dublin Book Festival 2026
Description:
Dublin Book Festival is one of Ireland’s biggest and most dynamic literature festivals, celebrating Ireland's writers, illustrators and publishers. With over 100 events taking place across 5 days in venues throughout Dublin City, featuring over 200 authors, illustrators, poets and musicians, the festival is packed with events for all ages. 

Events range from author in-conversations, panel discussions, book launches and literary walking tours, to creative workshops, professional development events, and a full free family and schools' programme. Genres explored range from contemporary fiction, history, nature and science, to poetry, non-fiction, art, wellbeing, children’s literature, and more. Many events free to attend.
Address: Royal Irish Academy of Music, 36-38 Westland Row, Dublin, Dublin

Name: Waterford Winterval 2026
Description:
Winterval 2026 will bring a mix of free and ticketed events including: 

Opening Event: The festival will kicks off with a large Christmas Parade and the official switching on of the lights by Santa

Waterford Eye & Fairground: A giant Ferris wheel on the quayside alongside vintage carousels and a helter-skelter.

Winterval Illuminates: A signature 3D light projection show, often located at Cathedral Square.

Christmas Markets: Artisan stalls featuring local crafts and food, primarily centered in the Waterford Cultural Quarter.

Ice Skating: The "Waterford on Ice" rink is a staple feature located on the city's quayside.

Santa Experiences: Immersive meet-and-greets, historically held in unique venues like the Medieval Museum.

Name: Sinéad Culbert: I’m No Wonder Woman
Description:
In her brand new stand up show, one half of comedy duo Dirt Birds,  Sinéad Culbert explores the extreme dangers of growing up in the 80’s, the pitfalls of parenting, the myths about marriage and the genuine joy of not giving a shit!

Dates/Times: Thurs 27th Oct 2026 @8pm-10:15pm including interval.
Tickets: €21.50+bf
Address: Siamsa Tíre - Theatre & Arts Centre, Town Park, Tralee, Kerry

Name: Bon Jovee ‘The Bon Jovi Tribute Show’
Description:
Relive the magic of Bon Jovi’s greatest hits which include “Livin on a prayer” and ” “You Give Love a Bad Name” and ” “Wanted Dead or Alive” “It’s My Life”, and countless others. Sing along to every word and feel the nostalgia wash over you as Bon Jovee takes you on a journey through the bands illustrious career.

Date(s)/Time(s): Sat 24th Oct 2026 @8pm-10:30pm including interval.
Tickets: General €27.50, Concession €25 +bf
Suitability: All ages
Address: Siamsa Tíre - Theatre & Arts Centre, Town Park, Tralee, Kerry

Name: Rory’s Stories: The Good Ol’ Days
Description:
Rory is back with his brand new comedy show The Good Ol’ Days, where he hitches a lift back to simpler times. Before social media, the only thing you needed to worry about was getting the torch shined on you at the teenage disco, village characters, knickknacks and cheering on Jackie’s Army. 


He will look at how life has changed and the new social norms; from shaving your nose hairs, being a coffee guru, enjoying nature walks and unfortunately having lots of responsibilities!

Date(s)/Time(s): Fri 16th Oct 2026 @8pm-10:15pm including interval.
Tickets: €28+bf
Suitability: 16yrs+
Address: Siamsa Tíre - Theatre & Arts Centre, Town Park, Tralee, Kerry

Name: Viking History & Celtic Mythology Walking Tour of Athlone
Description:
Hear the ancient tales of gods and goddesses who once roamed these sacred waters. From the mighty warrior Cuchulainn to the mystical goddess Boann, uncover the secrets and legends that have shaped the landscape for centuries. Walk in the footsteps of kings and heroes as we unravel the history of Athlone town. Learn about its origins, from its humble beginnings as a river crossing to its strategic importance in medieval times and beyond. 

Led by knowledgeable guides steeped in Celtic lore and local history, our walking tour promises to immerse you in the magic of Athlone like never before. Prepare to be spellbound by their captivating storytelling and deep insights into the town’s heritage.

Booking Essential. Price on request.
Address: Viking Tours Ireland, Castle St, Athlone, Westmeath

Name: EPIC Exhibition - Common Ground: Ireland in the EU
Description:
Ireland joined the European Economic Community (EEC) – as the EU was then known – on January 1, 1973, after a referendum endorsed by 83% of voters. It was then among the poorest and most underdeveloped countries in western Europe, with a population just over half of its current size.

Ireland’s accession proved to be the most consequential economic milestone in the half century since Irish independence, but it also set in motion far-reaching social and cultural change. EU legislation has driven improvements in workers’ rights, for example, and set binding targets for climate action. Irish people have studied and built new lives across Europe, while many Europeans have since made their homes here in Ireland.
Address: EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum, The Chq Building, Custom House Quay, North Wall, Dublin, Dublin

Name: Eric Lalor - Lol’er by Nature
Description:
Award-winning Eric Lalor is one of the most sought after comedians in the country. Some people will recognise him as the villain from Fair City, the gangster, Cathal Spillane. Name: B Walk – Deerpark to Nine Stones, Carlow Autumn Walking Festival 2026
Description:
The route begins in Kilbrannish Forest North, following a network of forest tracks through extensive woodland. As the walk progresses, participants will pass Deacon’s Wind Farm.

From here, the walk continues through Kilbrannish Forest North towards the scenic Corrabut Gap. The route then enters Kilbrannish Forest South, travelling through peaceful woodland environments, forest roads, and open clearings.

The walk concludes at the iconic Nine Stones, one of the best-known landmarks in the Blackstairs Mountains.

Suitable for experienced hill walkers, Walk includes:
Experienced members from Tullow Mountaineering Club leading the walk
Bus transport to/from the start/finish of your walk in Ballymurphy
Soup, sandwiches, tea and coffee after your walk
Address: Ballymurphy, Borris, Carlow

Name: B Walk – Ballycrystal to Scullogue Gap – Blackstairs Ridge Walk
Description:
The route climbs to Blackrock Mountain, from Blackrock then the trail follows the ridge to Mount Leinster, the highest point of the Blackstairs Mountains. 

The descent continues southwards to Knockroe, reaching its summit via another historic mountain track. From the top, you can take in views over the Barrow Valley and the southern reaches of the Blackstairs. Along the way, walkers will encounter the Dolmen known as the Giant’s Table.

The walk concludes as you follow Shannon’s Lane, winding down to the Scullogue Gap.

Suitable for experienced hill walkers, Walk includes:
Experienced members from Tullow Mountaineering Club
Bus transport to/from start/finish of walk
Soup, sandwiches, tea and coffee after the walk
Address: Rathanna Community Hall, Rathanna, Carlow

Name: Dublin by Dusk A Fair Exchange Writing Workshop
Description:
'A Fair Exchange' takes place in a series of locations in Collins Barracks, inviting new and exciting engagements with different exhibition spaces, themes, and collections. Facilitated by poet Hazel Hogan, you are invited to engage with the workshop in the following ways:

Read a participant’s story and take a moment to reflect.

Write your own response, inspired by a story, the space, or a historic object. Write, draw, sign, or remain anonymous.

Exchange your contribution by returning it to the vessel, helping grow a collective artwork of shared reflections.

Free drop-in workshop. All materials provided. No booking required. Wheelchair accessible.

Description:
This walk offers a unique opportunity to explore everything from conifer plantations and upland bogs to hedgerows and scrub, each a distinct wildlife habitat. 

As you traverse this scenic route, Éanna will introduce you to the birdlife of the area including chaffinches, ravens, robins & goldfinches, each with their distinct calls and songs. Her deep knowledge and passion for Ireland’s natural heritage will bring these landscapes to life, making this walk a real journey of discovery.

Description:
This 12km circular walk takes participants through some of the most scenic and historic landscapes in the region, with stunning views throughout the day.

Led by an experienced guide from Mountain Adventures, the route gradually ascends to a height of 795 metres, offering panoramic vistas across Carlow, Wexford and beyond. Along the way, walkers will visit the fascinating Moats of Craan, a remarkable archaeological feature steeped in local history, before continuing through areas rich in natural beauty and upland habitat.

The walk also passes the iconic Turfcutters Shed, a reminder of the traditions and heritage associated with life on the mountains.

Name: B Walk – Blackstairs Peaks, Carlow Autumn Walking Festival 2026
Description:
The mountain forms part of the natural boundary between Counties Carlow and Wexford and rewards walkers with magnificent views across Ireland’s south-east.

Caher Roe’s Den is steeped in local folklore. Caher Roe, a notorious highwayman often described as the Robin Hood of the Blackstairs, is said to have hidden his stolen treasure in a cave on this mountainside. Legend has it that some of his treasure remains concealed there to this day.

With its sweeping views, rugged mountain terrain and distinctive landmarks, this walk is an excellent choice for anyone wishing to experience the natural beauty and unique character of the Blackstairs Mountains.

Join us for a guided walk through the Blackstairs Mountains, where you’ll discover the fascinating history of the area. Led by knowledgeable local guides, this six-hour mountain trek offers a deep dive into the area’s ancient past, revealing the many stories etched into its rugged landscape. 

Ample time will be taken to pause and discuss the history and significance of these sites. Whether you’re a history enthusiast or simply curious about the past, this walk is a great opportunity to connect with the ancient heritage of this special area. 

Please note that normal hill walking gear is required for this walk.

Name: B Walk – Mount Leinster to Kildavin, Carlow Autumn Walking Festival 2026
Description:
From here the trail loops around Tomduff, before climbing to the cairn on Slievebawn, long associated with ancient ritual and tradition.

The walk then leads through the Corrabut Gap, a dramatic cut through the Blackstairs that has served for centuries as a passage between valleys. Your next ascent is Kilbrannish Hill. On clear days, walkers are rewarded with striking panoramas of the Barrow Valley below and the rolling ridges of the Blackstairs.

The final section follows the South Leinster Way, winding down through forest tracks and open farmland to the village of Kildavin, where the walk concludes.

Name: A Walk – Scullogue Gap Hike
Description:
Starting from the picturesque Scullogue Gap, this route leads you through some of the most stunning landscapes in County Carlow. 

The hike includes ascents of Mount Leinster, the highest peak in the Blackstairs range at 795 metres, offering panoramic views that stretch across eight counties including Carlow, Wexford and Kilkenny and on a fine day you can even glimpse the coast of Wales. You’ll also conquer Black Rock Mountain, known for its rugged beauty and dramatic terrain, as well as the Cloroge’s, a series of peaks that provide a fantastic vantage point for taking in the unspoiled countryside below.

Address: Rathanna, Carlow

Name: Diwali Delight
Description:

Name: Kilkenny's Toil & Trouble
Description:
Toil & Trouble is inspired by the extraordinary story of Alice Kyteler and Petronilla de Meath and one of Europe’s most infamous medieval witchcraft trials. Rooted in authentic witchcraft history and Irish Samhain traditions, the festival celebrates Kilkenny’s rich heritage through stories of folklore, myth, magic and the enduring power of place in one of Ireland’s most spectacular medieval cities.

Over four days, Toil & Trouble transforms Kilkenny into a stage for performances, literary events, family experiences, and outdoor animation. Name: Heroes of Tomorrow by Brokentalkers
Description:
Heroes of Tomorrow is the latest work from award-winning Brokentalkers, created in collaboration with acclaimed theatre-maker and writer Andy Smith. It is an epic story of how we got here and where we might go next. Through art, power and protest, it traces the forces that have shaped our world: oil, trade, weaponry, technology, colonialism and extraction.

A bold, fast-moving collision of history, politics and creativity, Heroes of Tomorrow also asks what happens when art meets power and what it might take to change the whole story.

The festival transforms the town, with events happening throughout the day and into the evening. From family activities at Halloween HQ in Pig Market Lane to live performances, creative workshops, immersive experiences and the spectacular Fire & Shadows Procession, there's something for everyone to enjoy.

Longford's Dead of Night Festival is the perfect way to experience the creativity, culture and community spirit of Longford Town during Spooky Season.

Suitable for all ages.

Brought to you by Samhain in the Heartlands, part of Ireland Home of Halloween. Go to Samhain in the Heartlands website for the full programme.

Readers are advised to check with the organiser before relying on the details published here.
Address: Longford, Longford

Name: Carlingford Food Tours
Description:
Great food, local stories, and a walk through one of Ireland’s most scenic coastal towns. This guided Carlingford food tour takes you through the heart of the medieval village with a selection of food and drink stops along the way, while your local guide shares the history, characters, and hidden corners that make Carlingford so special.

The tour begins on Carlingford Village Green and finishes at The Brass Door.

Various Saturdays in August - November | 2:30pm – 5:30pm

Name: Othello
Description:
Step into the gripping world of Shakespeare’s Othello, where love, loyalty and trust are put to the ultimate test. Othello is a celebrated military leader with a new marriage and a promising future but beneath the surface, resentment is beginning to grow. As friendships are tested and doubts begin to spread, the line between truth and deception becomes increasingly difficult to see. Packed with passion, tension, jealousy and betrayal, Othello is a powerful psychological drama about how quickly the people and relationships we trust can be turned against us. A timeless tragedy where nothing and no one is quite as they seem.

Sat 19 Sep + Sat 03 Oct

Name: The Lit Festival
Description:
Every year for one weekend, Ireland’s oldest city hosts Europe’s first youth-led literature festival! The Lit Festival returns to Waterford for its 9th edition with three days of workshops, performances and creative events for teens, young adults and families.

Discover Rap, Spoken Word & Activism with Mikey Cullen, Improv Theatre with Darren Yorke and Theatre Making with Niamh Fennessy. Join our Myth-Making in Modern Ireland panel with Ruth Ennis and Ellen Ryan, or share your stories at StorySlam! with Fighting Words Cork. Plus, explore as Gaeilge le Children's Books Ireland's Clinic Leabhair, a draw-along for U12s with Sarah Bowie and The Lit Does D&D – there’s something for every young person who wants to be part of a great story.
Address: Waterford

Name: The High Kings: The Power of the People Tour 2027
Description:
The momentum behind The High Kings continues to grow at an unprecedented pace, proving that folk music is not only alive and well, but thriving on a global stage.

Over the past two years, The High Kings have reached new heights, amassing millions of streams every week, selling out venues across Ireland, the UK, North America, Europe and Australia, and introducing a new generation of fans to the rich tradition of Irish folk music. Their music has transcended borders while remaining deeply rooted in Irish storytelling and heritage.

Name: Stories from the Sea from multiple-award winning film maker Ken O'Sullivan
Description:
From being surrounded by a pod of Killer whales to swimming with thousands of dolphins and fin and blue whales, the largest animals ever to have lived, Ken regales us with stories of the beauty of the natural world and our emotional connection with it.

Ken has produced more than 20 natural history documentaries for RTÉ and his last series NORTH ATLANTIC was acquired by BBC and broadcast in over 30 countries. He features alongside David Attenborough in BBC Earth’s STUNNING UNDERWATER NATURE FOOTAGE which has 7 million views on YouTube.

Adult €19 / Child & Concession €15 + Facility Fee / Family €60

Name: Dún Laoghaire Walking Tours 2027, The Dublin Riviera shore excursion
Description:
The Dublin Riviera is a guided coastal walk back to a golden era where local residents and visitors wined and dined in the yacht clubs, restaurants and hotels along the waterfront, and danced in the Pavilion, the ballrooms and the nightclubs. The walk will provide an insight into the symbiotic relationship between the harbour and the town and how this helped Dún Laoghaire to evolve into an elegant and glamorous centre of hospitality, entertainment and luxurious bathing, a “Dublin Riviera”.

Meeting Point:
Beside cruise passenger drop-off point at Quarterdeck

Highlights:
Waterfront Yacht Clubs and Royal Visits
The Pavilion and Town Hall
Royal Marine Hotel and Gardens
Haddington House Hotel
Former Seafront hotels 
Dún Laoghaire Baths
Address: Harbour Plaza, Harbour Rd, Dún Laoghaire, Dublin

The Dublin Riviera is a guided coastal walk back to a golden era where local residents and visitors wined and dined in the yacht clubs, restaurants and hotels along the waterfront, and danced in the Pavilion, the ballrooms and the nightclubs. The walk will provide an insight into the symbiotic relationship between the harbour and the town and how this helped Dún Laoghaire to evolve into an elegant and glamorous centre of hospitality, entertainment and luxurious bathing, a “Dublin Riviera”.

Meeting Point:
Beside cruise passenger drop-off point at Quarterdeck

Highlights:
Waterfront Yacht Clubs and Royal Visits
The Pavilion and Town Hall
Royal Marine Hotel and Gardens
Haddington House Hotel
Former Seafront hotels 
Dún Laoghaire Baths
Address: Harbour Plaza, Harbour Rd, Dún Laoghaire, Dublin

Name: The Chastitute
Description:
BTG presents John B. Keane’s hilarious and poignant comedy The Chastitute, co-directed by Charlie McGuinness and Ollie Kenny and dedicated to the memory of the late, great Gus Hanley. John Bosco McLaine is a 53-year-old bachelor farmer, celibate by force of circumstance and determined to find himself a bride. What follows is a wonderfully funny and awkward journey through matchmaking, mishaps and rural Irish life. A much-loved comedy, The Chastitute promises plenty of laughs and a great night’s entertainment.

Readers are advised to check with the venue before relying on the details published here.
Address: Backstage Theatre, Farneyhoogan, Farranyoogan, Longford

Name: Hayao Miyazaki's Dreams by Mystery Ensemble
Description:
The Miyazaki Dreams concert is an immersion in the fabulous atmosphere of the films of the world-famous Japanese director and Oscar winner Hayao Miyazaki. Mystery Ensemble has collected magical music from his anime and compositions inspired by his creations.

The evening programme includes renowned works composed by ingenious Joe Hisaishi, including My Neighbour Totoro, the legendary anime Spirited Away, Howl’s Moving Castle, Laputa: Castle in the Sky and others. 

Musical themes will transport viewers into the atmosphere of famous anime stories and introduce brave heroines, magical creatures, and characters inspired by Japanese folklore.

Readers are advised to check with the organiser before relying on the details published here.
Address: Father Mathew Quay, Centre, Cork

Name: Boyne Valley Dining Week 2026
Description:
Restaurants, cafés, pubs, hotels & food businesses throughout the region will put local produce centre stage with specially created dishes, seasonal menus, drinks pairings, tasting experiences and unique dining events. It’s the perfect opportunity to discover somewhere new, revisit a favourite venue & experience more of the fantastic food being produced right on your doorstep. 

From farmers & growers to bakers, brewers, distillers & artisan producers, Boyne Valley Dining Week celebrates the people & places behind our local food. Come hungry, explore the region and taste the Boyne Valley this October.

Name: Tim Burton's Universe by Mystery Ensemble
Description:
From the shimmering wonder of Alice in Wonderland to the festive magic of The Nightmare Before Christmas, from the haunting lyricism of Edward Scissorhands to the eccentric brilliance of Charlie and the Chocolate Factory, and including the darkly captivating world of Netflix's global phenomenon Wednesday, this concert immerses you in the soundscapes that shaped Burton’s unique cinematic universe. 

At the heart of it all is the music of Danny Elfman, Burton’s lifelong collaborator and one of the most distinctive film composers of our time. Elfman’s music blends playfulness with menace, tenderness with grandeur!

Performances at 5pm & 7pm

Readers are advised to check with the organiser before relying on the details published here.
Address: O'Reilly Theatre, 6 Denmark Street Great, Rotunda, Dublin, Dublin

Name: The Act of Existing
Description:
In this provocative new duet by Philip Connaughton for Croí Glan, two performers navigate shifting rules, unexpected choices and uncertain outcomes in a live encounter where observation and participation blur. Playful, unsettling and revealing, The Act of Existing explores how our choices, boundaries and expectations are shaped by those around us. As influence and responsibility come into focus, the work asks whether the simple act of being ourselves can become something profound.

For ages 18+

Readers are advised to check with the venue before relying on the details published here.
Address: Backstage Theatre, Farneyhoogan, Farranyoogan, Longford

Name: The Gates of the Otherworld: A Fantasy Dungeons & Dragons Adventure
Description:
Not only will you get to explore this land of myths and legends through the medium of D&D, but we will bring you to the ancient sites themselves so that you can see them with your own eyes and witness their majesty in person.

Our events are open to players of all experience levels and we encourage individuals, couples and groups to join us. Even if you don't bring friends with you, you will almost certainly leave with some.

This weekend-long TTRPG event will include:

Custom-written multi-session D&D adventure set in the ancient palace of Rathcroghan 
Accommodation for the weekend with a variety of sleeping options to suit all
3 meals a day including snacks and beverage
A special guest GM who will hosting some additional gaming activities
Address: Rathcroghan, Toberrory, Rathcroghan, Roscommon

Name: Lark After Dark: The Phantom of the Opera (1925)
Description:
More than a century after it first terrified audiences, the original 1925 The Phantom of the Opera returns to the big screen at The Lark.

Lon Chaney stars as the mysterious Phantom, haunting the hidden passages beneath the Paris Opera House in one of the defining films of early horror cinema.

With its vast gothic sets, theatrical atmosphere and one of cinema’s most famous unmasking scenes, this is a rare chance to experience a 100-year-old horror landmark as audiences originally did: on the big screen, together, in the darkness of a theatre.

Part of Lark After Dark: Home of Halloween in Balbriggan, Fingal.

Screenings at 7pm & 9pm. Tickets: €10 inc fees.

Readers are advised to check with the venue before relying on the details published here.
Address: The Lark Concert Hall, Church St, Balbriggan, Dublin

Name: Lark After Dark: House on Haunted Hill & Carnival of Souls
Description:
The night begins with Vincent Price in House on Haunted Hill (1959), as five strangers accept a chilling challenge to spend the night inside a supposedly haunted house.

After the interval, things get stranger with Carnival of Souls (1962). Following a mysterious accident, a young woman finds herself drawn to an abandoned carnival and haunted by an increasingly unsettling figure.

Two very different cult horror classics. One ticket. One night at the cinema.

Part of Lark After Dark: Home of Halloween at The Lark, Balbriggan, Fingal.
Both films are included in the €10 ticket. Starts 7pm.

Readers are advised to check with the venue before relying on the details published here.
Address: The Lark Concert Hall, Church St, Balbriggan, Fingal, Dublin

Name: Dave Elliott: Obsessed
Description:
Everyone nowadays claims they’re “obsessed” with everything – a TV show, a coffee, their friend’s new haircut. But let’s be honest… they’re not.
Dave, however, actually is.

In this hilarious new show, Dave dives head first into the things he’s irrationally obsessed with – the everyday annoyances, strange habits, petty grudges, and ridiculous details that no normal person should care this much about… but he absolutely does!

From social media nonsense to modern life’s weird unwritten rules, OBSESSED is a brutally funny deep dive into the tiny things that slowly drive us all insane.

Name: Eve Darcy: Married Without Children
Description:
Married Without Children explores society’s (i.e. Eve’s mother’s) expectations that women will get married and have kids, or at least will want to have kids. Eve doesn’t want to have kids. She’s not even sure she wants to be married!

Known for her engaging storytelling and incisive humour, Eve Darcy delivers a stand-up performance that is both laugh-out-loud funny and thoughtfully resonant. Married Without Children blends personal experience with cultural commentary, offering audiences an hour of comedy that challenges norms while celebrating autonomy, love and adult life on one’s own terms.

Address: Whelan's, 25 Wexford St, Portobello, Dublin, Dublin

Across a two-decade career, Diane has cultivated a devoted international following throughout Europe, Canada, and the United States. She has continually connected with audiences through new releases, extensive touring, and festival appearances at renowned events including Noise Pop, End of the Road, Green Man, Bergenfest, Pickathon, and Newport Folk Festival.

With a fresh new band and an eager fan base awaiting her return, Alela Diane is stepping back onto the road with new music and an exciting renewed sound.

The trail is fully accessible and suitable for all ages—ideal for family outings, date nights, or catch-ups with friends. Complete your visit at the Alpine-style food village with delicious treats, hot chocolate, and mulled wine.

Name: Mary Coughlan
Description:
Born in Shantalla, Galway city, Mary has made some of the most uncompromising, wholly personal, and universal music by any Irish artist. While her roots are in jazz and blues – Billie Holiday and Bessie Smith are among her inspirations – pop, rock, folk, and chanson (Edith Piaf is also a touchstone) influences also appear in her work. Now, the next chapter of her distinguished career finds her exploring a little known side of the music of Peggy Lee.

Never one to sit still, Mary is now planning her most ambitious project to date. While she has covered Billie Holiday, Joy Division, and The Blue Nile in the past, she intends to reimagine the album Peggy Lee made with the pioneering rock’n’roll songwriters Lieber and Stoller.
Address: dlr Mill Theatre Dundrum, 16 Sandyford Rd, Dundrum, Dublin, Dublin

Name: Gorey Whiskey Festival 2026
Description:
Gorey hosts its first whiskey festival on Friday 6 and Saturday 7 November 2026, a relaxed, multi-venue celebration of Irish whiskey in the heart of the town.

Presented by Gorey Whiskey Club, the weekend opens with a Friday evening club dinner and continues with a full Saturday programme of guided tastings and a whiskey-based cocktail event. Sessions run across Amber Springs Hotel, Browne's Lounge, Katie Daly's Bar and Paddy Blues Pub, all within walking distance of each other.

The programme features J.J. Corry, Killowen, Powerscourt, Boann, Two Stacks, Teeling and Echlinville. Each session is ticketed separately, so visitors can choose one event or build their own festival weekend.

Strictly for guests aged 18 and over.
Venue Name: Browne's Lounge and multiple venues across Gorey
Address: Browne's, 45 Main St, Gorey corporation lands, Gorey, Wexford

Name: Louise O'Neill: A Bigger Life
Description:
Dublin Book Festival is delighted to present an evening with award-winning author Louise O’Neill to celebrate her new memoir, A Bigger Life. At 38, Louise had the life she thought she wanted—until her long-term relationship ended, taking with it the home, future, and sense of certainty she’d built. Part memoir, part manifesto, A Bigger Life is a candid, courageous and funny look at dating, desire, rebuilding ourselves after heartbreak, and the radical act of wanting more. 

Join us for an evening of reflection, insight and uplifting humour as we consider the question at the heart of the book: What does it really mean to live a bigger life? Louise will join author Sophie White in conversation.
Address: 1WML, 1 Windmill Ln, Dublin, Dublin

Name: The Traitorous Tale: A Ghoulish Feast
Description:
As darkness falls, Malahide Castle takes on a sinister new atmosphere. The Traitorous Tale: A Ghoulish Feast is an immersive Samhain experience combining the castle’s dark history with live theatre, ancient traditions and an indulgent feast.  

The evening begins with a theatrical journey through the historic castle, where tales of betrayal, mystery and long-buried secrets unfold. The story continues over a delicious feast, surrounded by centuries of history and traditions associated with Samhain.

Part of the Home of Halloween initiative with Explore Fingal, this unique Halloween experience brings history and storytelling to life after dark, with theatrical encounters, unexpected twists and a few surprises along the way 👻
Address: Malahide Castle & Gardens, Back Rd, Malahide Demesne, Malahide, Dublin

Name: Directing for Theatre at the National Opera House
Description:
A director has to seamlessly combine the roles of dreamer and diviner with those of disciplinarian and driver of the process. The workshop will be an investigation of some of the key skills the successful director has to have: conceptual thinking for the setting and shaping of productions; text analysis for both contemporary and classic texts; rehearsal techniques to challenge and inspire a cast to give of their best. 

An enjoyable, highly informative, hands-on high-speed tour of these techniques, and more! This practical workshop for theatre practitioners is part of a series of multi-disciplinary development workshops hosted by Four Rivers Theatre Co.

Name: Tríona Marshall - Irish Harp
Description:
Playing with the mastery of a virtuoso and the voice of a storyteller the surprising depth of a single instrument is revealed.

Celebrated for the expressive depth and radiant tone of her playing, She brings together the worlds of Irish traditional, classical, and contemporary music. Her performances are marked by emotional clarity, subtle virtuosity, and a profound sense of connection with audiences.

Disappear Here Film Festival has consistently supported emerging and established voices through its annual programming, including fiction, documentary, animation and music video strands with 14 awards for individual films and the creatives behind them.

Description:

Name: Tríona Marshall - Irish Harp
Description:
Playing with the mastery of a virtuoso and the voice of a storyteller the surprising depth of a single instrument is revealed.

Celebrated for the expressive depth and radiant tone of her playing, She brings together the worlds of Irish traditional, classical, and contemporary music. Her performances are marked by emotional clarity, subtle virtuosity, and a profound sense of connection with audiences.

Name: EPIC Exhibition - Common Ground: Ireland in the EU
Description:
Ireland joined the European Economic Community (EEC) – as the EU was then known – on January 1, 1973, after a referendum endorsed by 83% of voters. It was then among the poorest and most underdeveloped countries in western Europe, with a population just over half of its current size.

Ireland’s accession proved to be the most consequential economic milestone in the half century since Irish independence, but it also set in motion far-reaching social and cultural change. EU legislation has driven improvements in workers’ rights, for example, and set binding targets for climate action. Irish people have studied and built new lives across Europe, while many Europeans have since made their homes here in Ireland.
Address: EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum, The Chq Building, Custom House Quay, North Wall, Dublin, Dublin

Name: EPIC Exhibition - Common Ground: Ireland in the EU
Description:
Ireland joined the European Economic Community (EEC) – as the EU was then known – on January 1, 1973, after a referendum endorsed by 83% of voters. It was then among the poorest and most underdeveloped countries in western Europe, with a population just over half of its current size.

Ireland’s accession proved to be the most consequential economic milestone in the half century since Irish independence, but it also set in motion far-reaching social and cultural change. EU legislation has driven improvements in workers’ rights, for example, and set binding targets for climate action. Irish people have studied and built new lives across Europe, while many Europeans have since made their homes here in Ireland.
Address: EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum, The Chq Building, Custom House Quay, North Wall, Dublin, Dublin

Name: Dublin by Dusk
Description:
Dublin by Dusk invites locals and visitors to enjoy the city centre in a new way on the last Thursday of each month. Participating venues and businesses will bring their own flavour to the evening, from late openings, tours and pop-up activities to cultural experiences, food and drink offers, shopping promotions and family-friendly options. It is a city-wide invitation to stay a little longer, discover something new and enjoy Dublin’s evening atmosphere across culture, hospitality, retail and visitor attractions.

The programme is supported by the Department of Culture, Communications and Sport, Dublin City Council, Fáilte Ireland and Dublin Town, working together with businesses and cultural partners to further re-energise the city centre.

Name: Ella Mai

Name: Midlands Fibre Festival
Description:
Come spend a day surrounded by yarn, colour, and creativity in the heart of Ireland at Ireland's newest yarn and fibre event. This festival is all about bringing fibre lovers together whether you knit, crochet, weave, embroider, spin, design, or just love yarn.

Name: Dublin by Dusk
Description:
Dublin by Dusk invites locals and visitors to enjoy the city centre in a new way on the last Thursday of each month. Name: Sneem International Storytelling & Folklore Festival 2026
Description:
Our festival is in its 13th year.  We have had visitors from USA, Hawaii, Europe, Australia and Ireland many of whom return annually. There are children's events, story swaps where you can tell your stories, two very interesting lectures, a concert by the local South Kerry Rosen Choir and Batt Burns Rambling House, you can even learn what Irish place names mean and how they came about. Weekend ticket €75 or pay as you go.

Name: Masters of Irish Art
Description:
Masters of Irish Art is a landmark exhibition celebrating Ireland's artistic heritage through an exceptional collection of original paintings by some of the nation's most important artists, including Jack B. Yeats, Paul Henry, Seán Keating and Roderic O'Conor, alongside leading contemporary Irish artists. 

Presented at The Oriel Gallery, established in 1968 and located beside the National Gallery of Ireland, the exhibition offers visitors a rare opportunity to experience museum-quality Irish art in one of Dublin's leading specialist galleries. 

With free admission, Masters of Irish Art invites visitors from Ireland and overseas to explore the stories, landscapes and cultural identity that have shaped Irish art across generations.
Address: 17 Clare St, Dublin, Dublin

Name: EPIC Exhibition - Common Ground: Ireland in the EU
Description:
Ireland joined the European Economic Community (EEC) – as the EU was then known – on January 1, 1973, after a referendum endorsed by 83% of voters. It was then among the poorest and most underdeveloped countries in western Europe, with a population just over half of its current size.

Ireland’s accession proved to be the most consequential economic milestone in the half century since Irish independence, but it also set in motion far-reaching social and cultural change. EU legislation has driven improvements in workers’ rights, for example, and set binding targets for climate action. Irish people have studied and built new lives across Europe, while many Europeans have since made their homes here in Ireland.
Address: EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum, The Chq Building, Custom House Quay, North Wall, Dublin, Dublin

Name: Feast of Samhain Cookery Class at Howth Castle
Description:
Celebrate the ancient festival of Samhain with a special hands-on evening cookery class at the award-winning Howth Castle Cookery School as part of Fingal's Home of Halloween Festival. 

Discover the rich flavours of autumn while exploring Ireland's culinary heritage through hearty root vegetable dishes, comforting seasonal recipes and traditional ingredients, all given a contemporary twist. Guided by our professional chefs, you'll prepare a delicious autumn feast before sitting down to enjoy your creations in the beautiful surroundings of historic Howth Castle. 

Perfect for food lovers, home cooks and anyone looking to celebrate Halloween with an authentic Irish flavour.

Wed 28 / Fri 30 Oct at 7pm.
Address: Howth Castle Cookery School, Howth Castle, Howth, Fingal, Dublin

Name: Samhain Sunday Brunch Cookery Class at Howth Castle
Description:
Celebrate the final day of the Samhain weekend with a hands-on autumn brunch experience at the award-winning Howth Castle Cookery School. Set within the magnificent 18th-century Georgian kitchen, guests will prepare a delicious seasonal menu inspired by the harvest, including roasted squash, warming spices, freshly baked treats and comforting autumn flavours. 

After cooking alongside our professional chefs, relax and enjoy your creations in the beautiful surroundings of historic Howth Castle. A unique culinary experience and a wonderful way to round off Fingal's Home of Halloween celebrations. 

Optional Extra: add a tour of the castle with our resident historian immediately after brunch.

Advance booking is essential.
Address: Howth Castle Cookery School, Howth Castle, Howth, Fingal, Dublin

After cooking, everyone will sit down together to enjoy their creations in the unique surroundings of historic Howth Castle. A memorable family experience as part of Fingal's Home of Halloween celebrations.

Name: Lourdes! The Musical by Xnthony

From the theatrical visionary behind the award-winning, five-star musical Oliver Cromwell is Really Very Sorry comes a sick new musical packed with holy bangers, emotional belters and a nun with a habit for DJing. Xnthony makes his second coming with Lourdes! The Musical which premieres at Dublin Theatre Festival this September and October, running at Civic Theatre, Tallaght. 
 
Lourdes! The Musical is an unexpected thrilling musical theatre extravaganza that needs to be seen, to be believed. Expect to laugh, cry, and emerge a fully changed person from this new stage pilgrimage where faith is spectacle and a ragtag troupe of pilgrims are staging an amateur musical about Saint Bernadette.

Name: Mystical Ireland – The Power of Ancient Cures and Curses
Description:
Healers are practicing a tradition that is thousands of years old but is in a very delicate state, whereby we could lose our cures within 20/30 years.  

Sarah McKenna Dunne’s 45 minute storytelling performance intertwines Irish mythology and her personal journey collecting stories from ordinary people who practice an extraordinary tradition. 

But as sure as cures have always existed, so too have curses, twined deeply with dark folklore, the desire to do harm invokes the land to betray its inhabitants. Sarah has encountered revenge caused by the act of curse, but thankfully she also knows where to get the cure of the curse for anyone who needs it!

Part of The Soul of Samhain and Home of Halloween at the Séamus Ennis Arts Centre, Fingal.
Address: The Séamus Ennis Arts Centre, Main St, Naul Village, Fingal, Dublin

Name: Herbs, Hexes and Halloween
Description:
This seasonal talk and workshop will explore the fascinating connection between witches and wise women healers in Irish history. You will also enjoy a wild herb tea tasting made from seasonal berries, seeds, and leaves while watching a demonstration on how to weave a protective Samhain Parshall cross from Rowan twigs and how to create a mugwort smudge stick.  

Part of The Soul of Samhain and Home of Halloween at the Séamus Ennis Arts Centre, Fingal.

Address: The Séamus Ennis Arts Centre, Main St, Naul Village, Fingal, Dublin

Name: Family Sourdough Pizza Making Workshop
Description:
Join in this interactive family workshop during the Harvest Food Fair where children and parents will discover the journey of food from the ground beneath our feet to a delicious homemade sourdough pizza.  Through fun activities, fascinating facts and hands-on-pizza making, young food explorers will learn how healthy soil helps grow health food, how farmers care for the land, and why the choices we make can help both our bodies and our planet.  

Ticket Price includes one parent and one child.

Part of The Soul of Samhain and Home of Halloween at the Séamus Ennis Arts Centre, Fingal.

Name: Spooky Comic Book Workshop
Description:
Dare to draw the Phantom Queen! In this spine-tingling comic workshop, young artists will dive into the magical and eerie world of Mór Riogain - the great shapeshifting queen of myth. Legend has it that she might appear as a mysterious woman, an ancient queen, or even a malicious raven. And whatever you do, don't let that raven land on your shoulder!

Perfect for kids who love a good scare and a great story, this workshop will teach aspiring comic creators how to bring ancient myths and creepy creatures to life on the page.

Grab your pencils/markers and paint and bring your bravest ideas. Just be careful who’s watching from the treetops!

Name: Halloween Fused Glass Kids Workshop
Description:
You can make it Halloween themed or go with your very own unique design.

Our instructor, Eddie will teach you about the process of fusing glass and then you will spend the rest of your time designing your masterpiece. Eddie will bring all the pieces home to be fired and when they are returned to the centre, all participants will be notified. 

This workshop is suitable for children aged 8+

Name: Cinderella Goes to The Halloween Ball Puppet Show
Description:
Ireland's travelling marionette theatre company Moon & Sixpence Puppet Theatre presents a magic pumpkin story for Halloween in a string puppet production of the classic fairy tale in the cheeky style of Moon & Sixpence productions. Cinderella's Halloween pumpkin transforms into a golden carriage, but Cinders prefers to travel to the Halloween Ball by hot air balloon instead! Meanwhile, her two ugly sisters can't decide if their Halloween masks actually make them less scary than usual! 

This colourful puppet production follows the traditional tale, but with messages about persistence, being yourself and not letting others bother you woven into the story.

Name: Samhain Tours of Howth Castle
Description:
Celebrate Samhain 2026 with a special ghostly guided tour of historic Howth Castle as part of Fingal's Home of Halloween Festival. Step inside one of Ireland's most iconic castles and uncover centuries of history and legends. As you explore the castle's atmospheric rooms and grounds, our resident historian will share captivating tales of ghostly encounters, remarkable characters and traditions linked to the origins of Halloween. 

Fingal Home of Halloween.

Suitable for families and history enthusiasts alike, this unique experience blends heritage and seasonal magic in an unforgettable setting. 

Meet at the front entrance of the castle 10 minutes before your tour begins. The tour starts outdoors, so please dress appropriately for the weather.
Address: Howth Castle, Howth Demesne, Fingal, Dublin

Name: Writing Workshop at Howth Castle – Samhain Festival
Description:
Meet other writers, write to prompts to generate new life stories, explore the themes of Samhain & Celtic culture, share your stories, receive feedback from Lara and together as a group, polish your favourite story of the week and leave with a finished story and many in the making. Explore writing using Irish words drawn from the beauty surrounding the castle. 

Literary presentation by historian-in-residence Daniel Eglinton-Carey
Walks to Aideen’s Grave & Howth fishing piers.

Final night: Hooks & Reels – evening of story & song at Howth Castle. 
October 31st 7-9.30pm. Chosen writers will present at the event. 

Part of Fingal's Ireland Home of Halloween.

Name: The Outcasts
Description:
The Outcasts, set in pre-famine Ireland when poverty and magic were rife, sees a young girl (Mary Ryan) discover a magical world of the imagination through ‘a wild, ungodly man’ (Mick Lally). When she is accused of witchcraft she uses her own supernatural powers for protection. Robert Wynne-Simmons combines horror, comedy and tragedy to produce this intelligent and visually stunning directorial debut.

Name: Savour Kilkenny Food Festival 2026
Description:
Savour Kilkenny Food Festival celebrates the rich culinary heritage and vibrant food culture of Ireland’s Ancient East that takes place at harvest end, also known as Samhain. Set against the stunning backdrop of Kilkenny Castle, this October bank holiday weekend event brings together top chefs, local artisan producers, and food enthusiasts from across the globe.

Visitors can explore a sprawling festival market featuring street food, craft beverages, and regional delicacies. Enjoy live cooking demonstrations, interactive workshops, masterclasses, and special dining experiences across Kilkenny’s finest restaurants. With plenty of family-friendly entertainment, Savour Kilkenny offers an unforgettable autumn celebration for every palate.

Description:
